title: DFlash: Block Diffusion for Flash Speculative Decoding
contribution: Lightweight 5-layer block-diffusion drafter that fills a 16-token masked block in one forward pass, conditioned on fused multi-layer target hidden states injected as extra K/V into every draft layer. Trained on target-generated responses with randomly anchored blocks and exponentially decaying per-position loss weights; shares the frozen target embedding/LM head.
limitation: Scope (experiments): speedup shrinks with concurrency (Qwen3-4B Math500 4.8x at c=1 to 2.9x at c=32) and the paper notes large blocks raise verification cost when compute-bound, leaving adaptive block-size scheduling to future work. Base drafter degrades beyond its 4K training context without long-context fine-tuning.
problem: Autoregressive drafting cost grows with draft length, capping drafter depth and speedup.
reported_tau: 9.1 (Qwen3.5-27B, HumanEval, block 16, SGLang c=8, App. Table 11); 7.87 on Qwen3-8B MATH-500, T=0 (Table 1)
targets_deep_positions: No: positions predicted independently; loss decay w_k=exp(-(k-1)/γ) deliberately emphasizes early positions.
per_position_analysis: No per-position curve; only notes block-8 drafter fully accepts 35.7% of blocks (Math500).
evidence: arXiv abstract + comments (ICML 2026 camera-ready); HTML Sec. 3-5, Tables 1-9; App. A.1-A.5 (Tables 10-13, vLLM Table 12)
notes: ID correct. Inco AI's DFlash 2 blog says the same team released DFlash in Jan 2026. DSpark and DFlash 2 measurements show DFlash's conditional acceptance drops sharply after position 1 then plateaus around 0.78-0.83.

title: DSpark: Confidence-Scheduled Speculative Decoding with Semi-Autoregressive Generation
contribution: Semi-AR drafter: DFlash parallel backbone plus a cheap sequential head (low-rank r=256 Markov transition bias from the previous sampled token, or a GRU-style RNN head) adding prefix-dependent logit bias while keeping exact per-token softmax probabilities. A calibrated confidence head (trained on 1-TV, sequential temperature scaling) drives a hardware-aware scheduler that picks per-request verification length to maximize expected accepted tokens x engine steps/s, with early stopping to stay lossless.
limitation: Paper-stated: the full γ-block draft cost is still paid upfront and is unrecoverable for low-acceptance queries. Scope: offline acceptance measured chain-only at T=1 on Qwen3/Gemma4 ≤14B; production uses γ=5 with an asynchronous scheduler whose losslessness argument relies on two-step-stale confidences.
problem: Parallel drafters' suffix decay; fixed-length verification wastes batch capacity at high load.
reported_tau: 6.21 (Qwen3-14B, GSM8K, γ=7, T=1, chain, Table 1); ~7.6 at draft length 16 (RNN head, Qwen3-4B math, Fig. 4, read from plot)
targets_deep_positions: Yes: Markov/RNN head conditions each token on sampled predecessors; gain over DFlash grows 16%→30% from γ=7 to γ=15.
per_position_analysis: Yes (Fig. 2, conditional, Qwen3-4B, T=1): DFlash drops after pos 1 then plateaus; EAGLE-3 rises; DSpark flat-high.
evidence: arXiv abstract; HTML Sec. 3-5 (Alg. 1, Table 1, Figs. 2, 4, 7, 8, Limitations); Fig. 2/4/8 rendered from arXiv HTML assets
notes: Own acceptance-by-position (Fig. 2, γ=7, values read from plot): Math DFlash .885→.83→.82-.84, EAGLE-3 .81→.85, DSpark .905→.88 (text claims .93 start); Code DFlash .865→.815→.78, EAGLE-3 .77→.785, DSpark .886→.851; Chat DFlash .717→.648→.687, EAGLE-3 .533→.733, DSpark .735→.761. Fig. 4: DFlash τ saturates from draft length 12→16 (math 5.4→5.5) while DSpark keeps rising (6.6→7.2 Markov, ~7.6 RNN). Draft length 16 = anchor + 15 proposals. Max batch: live DeepSeek-V4 traffic up to ~200 concurrent requests/engine (Fig. 8; scheduler shrinks verification budget from ~5-6 to ~3.5 tokens as load rises); latency study at batch 128.

title: P-EAGLE: Parallel-Drafting EAGLE with Scalable Training
contribution: Turns EAGLE into a one-pass multi-token drafter: positions after the first use a learnable shared hidden state plus a learned mask-token embedding (unfrozen embeddings, 4 layers). Makes long-context (up to 20K) parallel-prediction training feasible via precomputed sliceable attention masks and within-sequence partitioning for gradient accumulation under COD.
limitation: Scope (experiments): gains over EAGLE-3 are modest (1.0-1.36x) and shrink at concurrency 4 for large/MoE targets as verification dominates; evaluated only up to C=4, K≤7, chain drafting on one H200. No intra-block dependency modeling; acceptance only matches AR EAGLE-3.
problem: EAGLE needs K sequential passes; parallel-drafter training is infeasible at long contexts.
skill: Shared hidden state; scalable parallel training
reported_tau: 4.5 (Qwen3-Coder-30B, HumanEval, K=5, Table 9)
targets_deep_positions: No: all later positions share one learned hidden state; position-specific encodings hurt by 7-15%.
evidence: arXiv abstract; HTML Sec. 2-5 (Tables 1-10), App. C (Table 11)
notes: ID correct. Trained with K_train=8, inference K≤7 (training at 8 beats 5 by ~4%). Sampling temperature not stated. Only aggregate MTP-position accuracy (57.9%) reported, no per-position acceptance.

title: PARD: Accelerating LLM Inference with Low-Cost PARallel Draft Model Adaptation
contribution: Adapts a small standalone AR LM into a target-independent parallel drafter that predicts K future tokens in one pass using a shared mask token (extrapolates to K_infer > K_train). Conditional Drop-token (COD) training keeps geometrically fewer positions at deeper prediction depths while preserving prefix KV integrity, cutting adaptation cost ~3x.
limitation: Scope (experiments): speedup falls steeply with batch (3.63x at bs=1 to 1.33x at bs=16 on Llama3.1-8B) and throughput peaks at K_infer=12, dropping at 16. No target features or intra-block dependency, so deep positions decay (PARD-2 Fig. 2a).
problem: Target-specific draft heads are costly to train; AR small drafters are slow.
reported_tau: Not reported in PARD (gives 1-α/4-α = 0.93/0.90 on HumanEval, plus TPS); PARD-2 Table 1 measures PARD at 6.71 (Llama3.1-8B HumanEval, K=16, T=0)
targets_deep_positions: No: positions independent given prefix and masks; COD reduces supervision at deeper positions.
per_position_analysis: Only average acceptance at draft length 1 vs 4 (Table 2: 0.93 vs 0.90 HumanEval); no per-position curve.
evidence: arXiv abstract (v4); HTML Sec. 3-4 (Tables 1-3, Fig. 5b rendered), App. D (Table 5); GitHub AMD-AGI/PARD README news
notes: ID correct. Venue: repo README news 'PARD is accepted to ICLR'26' (2026-01-26) and DSpark bibliography (ICLR 2026, OpenReview XbOyv7iVGL); arXiv comment still says 'submitted for possible publication'. Drafter is a separate small LM (e.g., Llama-3.2-1B) shared across a model family; K_train=8 default. Temperature not stated.

title: PARD-2: Target-Aligned Parallel Draft Model for Dual-Mode Speculative Decoding
contribution: Confidence-Adaptive Token (CAT) loss weights each future-token CE+KD term by the cumulative product of target confidences along the ground-truth prefix, a proxy for the probability that position is reached in verification. Stochastic gating of fused target hidden features lets one standalone PARD-style drafter run in target-dependent or target-independent mode.
limitation: Scope (experiments): all acceptance results are greedy (T=0) chain decoding with tree disabled, on Llama3.1-8B/Qwen3 ≤32B with A100s; no limitations section. The deep-position comparison vs PARD confounds CAT with a longer training horizon (K=16 vs PARD's 8).
problem: Uniform or fixed-decay position losses misalign training with consecutive-acceptance objective.
reported_tau: 9.19 (Llama3.1-8B, HumanEval, K=16, T=0, target-dependent mode, Table 1)
targets_deep_positions: Yes, indirectly: CAT weights loss by estimated prefix survival; per-position acceptance stays ~0.91-0.94 to position 16.
per_position_analysis: Yes (Fig. 2a, HumanEval, Llama3.1-8B): PARD decays 0.92→0.47 by pos 16; PARD-2 stays flat ~0.91-0.94.
evidence: arXiv abstract; HTML Sec. 3-4 (Tables 1-5); Figs. 1-2 rendered from arXiv HTML assets
notes: ID correct. Fig. 2a cumulative τ: PARD saturates ~6.6 by pos 12, PARD-2 keeps rising to ~9.2 at pos 16. PARD's official drafter was trained at K=8, so its collapse after pos ~9 is partly extrapolation. vLLM batch sweep 1-64 (Fig. 1): PARD-2 above PARD and EAGLE-3 at every batch size (~3.9k vs 2.8k TPS/GPU AR at bs=64).

title: DART: Diffusion-Inspired Speculative Decoding for Fast LLM Inference
contribution: Single-layer drafter on fused target hidden states appends d-1 mask tokens and emits d shifted next-token logits in one pass (causal mask within the block), trained with prefix-shared masks and annealed KL (γ=0.6). Builds the draft tree by beam search over per-position top-k combining draft log-prob with an N-gram continuity score.
limitation: Scope (no limitations section): designed for a short horizon (d=8) with early-position emphasis, and τ (~3.6-4.1) does not beat EAGLE-3's; speedup decays to 1.45x at batch 64.
problem: EAGLE-3 multi-step AR rollout makes drafting the latency bottleneck.
reported_tau: 4.08 mean (LLaMA2-Chat-7B, T=0, d=8 tree, Table 1); up to 4.59 on CodeAlpaca (N-gram ablation, Table 2)
targets_deep_positions: No: KL annealing favors early positions; only N-gram continuity scoring couples adjacent tokens during tree pruning.
per_position_analysis: Yes (Table 4): unconditional top-1 accuracy per future position decays steeply, 75.5%→44.7%→29%→19%→13.8%→11.2%.
evidence: arXiv abstract; HTML Sec. 3-5 (Alg. 1, Tables 1-5)
notes: ID correct. ICML-style template but no acceptance evidence found. Per-position numbers are marginal accuracy vs ground truth, not conditional acceptance. Domino measures public DART checkpoints (60-node tree) at τ≈2.6-3.0 on Qwen3.

title: Domino: Decoupling Causal Modeling from Autoregressive Drafting in Speculative Decoding
contribution: Adds to a DFlash backbone a 'Domino head': a GRU (d=1024) over embeddings of previously sampled draft tokens plus a low-rank (r=256) logit-space residual correction, run as a fused cheap sequential loop. Trained teacher-forced with a base-anchored curriculum that anneals loss weight from backbone logits to corrected logits to prevent backbone collapse.
limitation: Paper-stated: targets inference rather than training cost, implementation mainly adapted to SGLang, and speedup varies across hardware. Scope: Qwen3-4B/8B only, concurrency ≤32, and headline tables compare against public DFlash checkpoints trained on different data.
problem: Parallel drafters lose intra-block causal dependencies; AR drafters pay sequential cost.
reported_tau: 10.12 (Qwen3-4B, GSM8K, block 16, T=0, Transformers backend, Table 1)
targets_deep_positions: Yes: GRU state over sampled predecessors corrects every later position's logits; no per-position evidence shown.
evidence: arXiv abstract; HTML Sec. 4-5 (Tables 1-4, Fig. 4), Limitations, App. A (Tables 5-6)
notes: ID correct. Same-data (ShareGPT) ablation: EAGLE-3 τ 5.01 > Domino 4.65 > DFlash 3.90 on GSM8K, yet Domino is fastest. Head on/off ablation: τ 3.49→4.19 (+20%). At c=32 speedups compress to 1.9-2.1x (EAGLE-3 60-node tree 0.4x).

title: xPress: Parallel Refinement for Diffusion Drafters in Speculative Decoding
contribution: Low-rank (r=256) causal refiner that fuses each position's drafter hidden state, a block-mean summary and the previous token, mixes them with per-channel strictly lower-triangular weights, and reads out an additive logit bias on DFlash logits. The dependency is resolved with K≈4-7 parallel Jacobi iterations (provably reaching the sequential greedy fixed point), trained with CE + TV loss plus drafter-anchor and drafter-seeded consistency terms.
limitation: Paper-stated: Jacobi iteration count K is fixed per run; adaptive per-block stopping is future work. Scope: single target (Qwen3-8B) and drafter (DFlash b16), vLLM batch ≤32 greedy only; T=1 handling of the Jacobi refinement is not detailed.
problem: Diffusion drafter emits independent marginals, causing early rejection of jointly incoherent blocks.
reported_tau: 10.13 (Qwen3-8B, GSM8K, block 16, greedy, vLLM, Table 2); avg 8.02 at T=0 and 6.97 at T=1 (Table 1)
targets_deep_positions: Yes: each position conditions on all sampled predecessors via the causal mixer; +30% avg τ (up to +56%) over DFlash.
per_position_analysis: No per-position curve; only τ vs Jacobi iterations K (plateau by K≈7).
evidence: arXiv abstract; HTML Sec. 4-5 (Tables 1-3, Figs. 3-4), Conclusion
notes: ID correct. DSpark Markov head retrained under identical recipe: avg τ 7.64 vs xPress 8.02 vs DFlash 6.25 (T=0); gains larger at T=1 (1.46x throughput over DFlash). τ and the 1.2-1.4x edge over DFlash are batch-invariant at bs 16-32.

title: TreeFlash: Parallel AR-Approximation for Faster Speculative Decoding
contribution: Adds a SwiGLU 'AR-approximator' that updates each DFlash position's hidden state with the embedding of the preceding token, giving bigram-conditioned per-node distributions. Keeps O(1) drafting via two stages: build a top-M-ary tree from DFlash marginals, evaluate the approximator on its M·γ unique (token, position) pairs in parallel, then select an OPT-Tree; trained with forward KL from a DFlash initialization.
limitation: Paper-stated: all experiments single-batch with SDPA (large dynamic trees may conflict with multi-batch serving), initialized from DFlash, teacher-forced exposure bias, Qwen-only. Non-leaf tree nodes must lie inside the top-M tree.
problem: One-shot drafters' marginals diverge from AR distribution with depth, worse in trees.
reported_tau: 11.02 (Qwen3-8B, MATH-500, T=0, tree budget 64, Table 1); mean 9.71 at budget 512 (Qwen3-4B greedy, Fig. 5)
targets_deep_positions: Yes: previous-token conditioning cuts depth-15 TVD to verifier from 0.81 to 0.62; gain over DDTree grows with budget.
per_position_analysis: Yes (Figs. 3-4): TVD vs depth rises steadily (DFlash 0.19→0.81); top-K coverage decays; TreeFlash slower.
evidence: arXiv abstract; HTML Sec. 3-4 (Tables 1-3, Figs. 3-6), Limitations
notes: ID correct. Verification is an equality check against the target's (sampled) token, lossless at T=1. Most gain over DFlash comes from chain→tree (DDTree ≈63% of τ gain); AR-approx adds +7.5% τ (B=16) to +12.4% (B=64). Beyond depth 9 even the true marginal has higher TVD than TreeFlash. Tree budgets up to 512 nodes.

title: DBLAST: Dependent Block Drafting for Stochastic Speculative Decoding
contribution: Adds a K-way categorical latent (CP-style low-rank mixture) to a DFlash drafter: a linear expander yields K category-specific hidden branches and a prior head picks the category, so positions are correlated through the shared mode while still decoded in one pass; verification uses the exact prefix-marginalized mixture conditional. Trains with an accepted-length log surrogate summed over threshold-truncated prefixes.
limitation: Paper-stated: the surrogate is neither unbiased nor a bound, the soft-mixture training vs greedy-branch inference gap is uncharacterized, and training-data stochasticity is unexplored. Scope: reports accepted length only (no end-to-end speedup), ≤256 generated tokens, Qwen3-4B/8B, batch-1 latency.
problem: Independent block sampling loses acceptance as target sampling entropy increases.
reported_tau: 6.29 accepted tokens excl. bonus (≈7.3 incl.) (Qwen3-4B, GSM8K, T=0.7/top-p 0.8, Table 2)
targets_deep_positions: Yes, indirectly: shared latent mode makes later tokens consistent with earlier ones; biggest gains at high target entropy.
evidence: arXiv abstract; HTML Sec. 3-6 (Tables 1-4, Figs. 1-2), App. B-E (Tables 5-8)
notes: ID correct (HTML title spells 'DBLast'). Gain over DFlash rises 5.6%→12.1% (Qwen3-8B) as target sampling goes T=0.7→1.5; K=4 adds ~1.4-1.6% latency. Proposal is a prior-weighted mixture of K greedy branches (sparse q); only T>0 evaluated.

title: LiLiCorr: Lightweight Likelihood Correlation of Parallel Drafts for Speculative Decoding
contribution: Keeps DFlash's top-8 candidates per slot and runs a 2-layer bidirectional transformer over the whole (B-1)xK candidate lattice, emitting unit in/out vectors per candidate; adjacent-slot cosine scores give locally normalized transitions and a weight-free greedy argmax walk commits one path. Co-trained with DFlash using oracle-prefix CE plus a target-weighted distractor penalty.
limitation: Paper-stated: only reranks the drafter's top-K, so acceptance is bounded by candidate coverage, and only adjacent slots are coupled. Scope: Qwen3-4B/8B, block 16, concurrency ≤32 on one H100.
problem: Per-slot marginal training yields individually plausible but jointly incoherent blocks.
reported_tau: 9.06 (Qwen3-8B, MATH-500, greedy, c=1, App. Table 5); 9.24 with DFlash2-style conv added
targets_deep_positions: Yes: each slot's pick conditions on the committed predecessor via whole-lattice-aware pair scores; no per-position data.
evidence: arXiv abstract (v2); HTML Sec. 3-5 (Tables 1-2), App. A-G (Tables 3-17)
notes: ID correct (v2 2026-09-22). Matched-training head-to-head (Qwen3-8B, greedy avg τ): LiLiCorr 6.44, DSpark 6.40, Domino 6.30, DFlash2 6.27 vs DFlash 5.59; DSpark has longest τ at T=1 sampled but serves slower (head 0.78 vs 0.30 ms/block). τ changes only -1.4%..+0.5% from c=1 to c=32. Exact Viterbi path decodes 2.6% worse than the greedy walk. DFlash2 baseline is a third-party reimplementation.

title: JetSpec: Breaking the Scaling Ceiling of Speculative Decoding with Parallel Tree Drafting
contribution: DFlash-style head (KV-injected target features) with a block-causal mask so each draft position attends only to the prefix and earlier draft positions, trained by forward-KL distillation. Builds best-first trees (top-W per depth, cumulative log-prob scoring) up to 256 nodes and integrates tree verification into vLLM with a custom paged tree-attention kernel.
limitation: Scope (paper's serving data): large tree budgets pay only at low load (budget 128 best at bs=1 but worst at bs=16, where budget 32 wins), with dynamic budget scheduling left to future work. vLLM path is greedy-only, and at budget 16 JetSpec merely matches DFlash.
problem: Bidirectional block marginals form inconsistent trees; AR tree drafting cost grows with depth.
reported_tau: 10.76 (Qwen3-8B, MATH-500, T=0, tree budget 256, Table 2); 10.65 on Qwen3-30B-A3B (Table 5)
targets_deep_positions: Yes, weakly: causal mask over draft hidden states, but per-depth candidates stay branch-agnostic (ignore sampled tokens).
per_position_analysis: No per-position curve; branch-level log-prob gap case study (App. A).
evidence: arXiv abstract (v5); HTML Sec. 3-4 (Tables 1-7), App. B-E (Alg. 1, Tables 10-11)
notes: ID correct; 5 versions (latest 2026-10-03). Main-table DFlash/DDTree baselines were trained without loss decay; with DFlash's decay (γ=7) the diffusion head nearly matches the causal head (τ 9.72 vs 9.99, Table 7), so the causal-mask gain itself is small. Reverse-KL distillation drops τ 36-46%.

title: DiffuSpec: Unlocking Diffusion Language Models for Speculative Decoding
contribution: Training-free use of a pretrained 7B dLLM (Dream-7B) as a one-pass drafter. Causal-consistency path search beam-searches an entropy-pruned per-position candidate lattice scored by DLM log-prob plus a 3-gram causal proxy, and an adaptive draft-length controller sets the next block size from EOS-aware generation and acceptance EMAs.
limitation: Paper-stated future work: DLM drafting lacks KV reuse/fused kernels and the causal proxy is weak. Scope: greedy-only (T=0), batch 1, single A100, one 32B target with a memory-heavy 7B drafter.
problem: AR drafters are sequential; dLLM lattices are not left-to-right consistent; preset length.
skill: Causal path search, adaptive draft length
reported_tau: 6.99 mean accepted tokens (Qwen2.5-32B target, Dream-7B drafter, Spec-Bench, greedy, Table 1); 7.33 with 10 refinement steps (slower)
targets_deep_positions: Yes, indirectly: n-gram-guided lattice path search pushes first mismatch rightward; ADL avoids oversized blocks.
per_position_analysis: No per-position curve; MAT vs fixed draft length plateaus (6.49 at k=30, 6.69 at k=100).
evidence: arXiv abstract; HTML Sec. 4-5 (Tables 1-2, Fig. 7), App. C (Table 5); ACL Anthology 2026.findings-acl.1048
notes: ID correct; v1 dated 2025-09-28 although id is 2510. Acceptance ratio uses an L2R masked proxy q while the token is chosen by beam search; only T=0 evaluated, so losslessness under sampling is not demonstrated. ADL operates in k∈[20,30].

title: SpecDiff-2: Scaling Diffusion Drafter Alignment For Faster Speculative Decoding
contribution: Streak-distillation fine-tunes a 7B discrete-diffusion drafter to maximize a pathwise surrogate of expected accepted streak (sum over m of products of drafter marginals on verifier-sampled paths). Self-selection samples K drafts from one pass's marginals, scores all with verifier conditionals in one tree-attention pass, and verifies the best with point-mass acceptance (accept w.p. p(x), residual excludes x).
limitation: Paper-stated: formal analysis of the greedy-acceptance rule and the optimal diffusion-drafter size remain open, and kernels/KV caching for diffusion drafts are lacking. Scope: 7B drafters too slow for 13-14B verifiers; batch size never reported.
problem: Diffusion drafter marginals misaligned with AR verifier, worst at later window positions.
reported_tau: 7.71 tokens/draft incl. bonus (Qwen2.5-72B, HumanEval, T=1, DiffuCoder-7B drafter, γ=32, Table 2)
targets_deep_positions: Yes: streak objective weights later window positions by survival; 3.2x higher later-position acceptance than AR-style distillation.
per_position_analysis: Yes (Fig. 2, γ=32): α_j decays steeply then plateaus (~0.16 streak-distill vs ~0.06 AR-distill, ~0.03 base).
evidence: arXiv abstract; HTML Sec. 3-7 (Figs. 2, 5, 10; Tables 2-3), App. A-B; MLSys 2026 oral page (mlsys.org/virtual/2026/oral/3755)
notes: ID correct. Main γ=32 (DiffuCoder) / 16 (DiffuLLaMA); γ ablation 8-128 (unaligned SpecDiff) peaks at 32. Point-mass acceptance after verifier-based selection is still lossless (selection uses distributions, not verifier coin flips). Batch size unknown (2xA100 for 70B+).

title: D^2SD: Accelerating Speculative Decoding with Dual Diffusion Draft Models
contribution: Uses DFlash's calibrated per-position confidences to form a posterior over the rejection boundary, r(i)=Π_{k≤i}c_k·(1-c_{i+1}), and picks the top-K boundaries. A second variable-prefix diffusion drafter (trained with a geometric prefix-length prior and anchor-relative loss decay) re-anchors at each boundary and redrafts the suffix in one batched pass; the K+1 shared-prefix candidates are verified with cascade attention.
limitation: Scope (no limitations section): no batch>1 or serving-engine results, and a third cascade level raises τ 8% but cuts speed 4%. Sampling (T=1) gains are small on GPT-OSS-20B and the multi-branch T=1 acceptance rule is not specified.
problem: Single diffusion block wasted after first mismatch; bigger blocks and resampling don't help.
skill: Re-anchored second drafter at rejection points
reported_tau: 11.94 (GPT-OSS-20B, MBPP, T=0, γ=16, K=4, Table 4); Qwen3-8B avg 7.05 vs DFlash 5.31 (Table 3)
targets_deep_positions: Yes: re-drafts the suffix after predicted rejection points with a drafter conditioned on the realized prefix.
per_position_analysis: No per-position curve; DFlash τ vs block size saturates at 16-24 and drops at 32 (Table 1).
evidence: arXiv abstract; HTML Sec. 1-4 (Tables 1-7, Fig. 2)
notes: ID correct. D²SD itself uses γ=16; 32 appears only in the DFlash block-size study (Qwen3-8B MATH-500 TPF 5.04/6.05/6.01/5.85 at γ=8/16/24/32, decay-matched training). K naive resampled branches from the same DFlash pass add only +0.33-0.37 τ; reusing DFlash as second drafter gives +14% vs +33% with the VP-drafter. Batch size not reported.

title: PRESTO: Prefix-Aligned Tree Drafting for Diffusion Speculative Decoding
contribution: Training-free tree drafting for diffusion drafters: each candidate is rescored as log q_d(t) + λ·log ρ_d(t|prefix) with a 3-gram prefix model (λ≈0.2), then expanded by beam search with global retention or best-first search to budgets of 128-1024 nodes. Also extends tree drafting to self-speculative dLLMs (Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion, linear and quadratic modes).
limitation: Paper-stated: the n-gram prefix signal is only short-range, and evaluation is mostly single-request in PyTorch with larger batches/production engines untested. Scope: tree budgets kept ≤512 to stay memory-bound.
problem: Linear diffusion drafting wastes candidates; prefix-blind marginals mis-rank tree paths.
reported_tau: 11.1 (Qwen3-8B DFlash, MATH-500, T=0, Table 2); 13.2 on Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion-8B linear self-speculation (MATH-500, T=0, Table 3)
targets_deep_positions: Yes, indirectly: n-gram prefix rescoring plus tree hedging raises full-block acceptance; no position-specific mechanism.
per_position_analysis: No per-position curve; acceptance-length histograms shift toward full-block; top-10 oracle bound (GSM8K 6.5→9.78).
evidence: arXiv abstract; HTML Sec. 3-6 (Tables 1-4, Figs. 2, 4), Limitations
notes: ID correct but v1 is dated 2026-06-20 while the id is 2607 (announced July 2026). DFlash block 16; NLD speculative block/tree budget 32. Shares first author (Zheng Wang) with xPress.

title: DFlash 2: Keep Drafting Parallel
contribution: Path selector keeps the top-16 candidates per position and scores adjacent pairs S_t(a,b)=U_t(b)+⟨A(a)⊙H(h_t),B(b)⟩ (256-d token embeddings with a context gate), then walks greedily or samples from the precomputed scores (+2M params, +0.6% latency). Two-tap dynamic causal depthwise convolutions before/after each sublayer let every position read its predecessor in parallel (+3% params), shrinking suffix decay.
limitation: Scope (blog/model card, vendor-run): no paper or disclosed training recipe, and all numbers are Inco AI's own SGLang tests at concurrency ≤32. At concurrency 32 (Qwen3.8-27B, block 8) speedup falls to 1.01-1.45x.
problem: Independent DFlash picks are jointly incoherent; suffix decay toward block end.
reported_tau: 6.76 (Qwen3.5-4B, MATH-500, T=1 thinking, block 16, blog Table 3); mean 5.97 vs DFlash 4.92 / DSpark 5.49
targets_deep_positions: Yes: two-tap causal conv curbs suffix decay; selector conditions on chosen predecessor; flat ~86% conditional acceptance to position 14.
per_position_analysis: Yes: conditional Recall@1/@16 and conditional acceptance by position; DFlash dips after pos 0, DFlash 2 flat ~85-86%.
evidence: inco.ai/blog/dflash2 (Aug 18 2026; Tables 1-5, Figs. 2, 5); HF model card incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 (concurrency 1/8/32 tables)
notes: Not a paper; z-lab mirrors the checkpoints. Qwen3-4B DFlash (5L, GSM8K) conditional Recall@1 85.4→72.9% and Recall@16 99.5→87.8% over positions 0-6; an oracle top-16 path would lift τ 4.27→6.79. Conditional acceptance (Qwen3.5-4B MATH-500, T=1): DFlash 88.4→77.7→77.5%, DSpark 87.2→79.9%, MTP 84.6→77.9%, DFlash 2 88.3→86.5%. Recall@1 at pos 6: 5L 72.9%, 5L+conv 77.6%, 15L 78.7%. At c=32 MTP/DSpark drop to 0.74-1.13x. LiLiCorr reports the DFlash2 training recipe is undisclosed.

title: Accelerating Speculative Decoding with Block Diffusion Draft Trees
contribution: Builds a draft tree from one DFlash pass by taking the B highest-probability prefixes under the factorized per-position marginals (provably optimal for that surrogate), found with a best-first heap. The tree is verified in one target pass with an ancestor-only mask by walking the target's own greedy/sampled token.
limitation: Scope (no limitations section): single-stream HF Transformers harness at batch 1 with SDPA tree attention on Qwen3-4B/8B/Coder-30B-A3B. Node scores are unconditioned marginals, and the budget is picked per cell from 16-1024 (speedup peaks at 256-512 on H200).
problem: DFlash verifies one trajectory per round, discarding its other per-position candidates.
reported_tau: 10.73 (Qwen3-8B, MATH-500, T=0, best budget; incl. bonus token); 10.72 Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B HumanEval
targets_deep_positions: no; factorized marginals leave deep nodes unconditioned; more full-block acceptances come from hedging early positions.
per_position_analysis: Acceptance-length histogram only: mass shifts to long prefixes, more full 16-token acceptances; no per-depth rates.
evidence: abs page; HTML Sec. 3-5 (Table 1, Figs. 3-4), App. B
notes: ID correct. At T=1 the target's sampled token is walked through a deterministic tree (lossless, no rejection sampling). Batch size never mentioned; 1 inferred from the HF single-sequence harness. No venue found (project page cites arXiv).

title: CAST: Cost-Aware Speculative Trees from One-Pass Block Drafters
contribution: Packs the top-N path-product prefixes of an unchanged DFlash block into a tree and keeps adding candidates while their mass exceeds a measured verify-time 'token-time exchange rate', so width adapts to GPU/kernel cost without sweeps. Extends the rule to a batch-shared budget via global best-first allocation across requests with a ragged (varlen) Triton tree-verify kernel.
limitation: Own: the tree is optimal only inside a K=8 universe of a non-path-conditioned marginal belief, so deeper branches stay exposed to calibration error; timing is decode-only steady state, not a serving-throughput claim. Scope: dense targets up to 8B plus one 30B-A3B MoE; main runs at batch 1.
problem: Block decoders discard already-scored candidates; best tree width varies with GPU and load.
reported_tau: 9.87 committed round length (Qwen3-8B, MATH-500, T=0, N*=127, H100)
targets_deep_positions: no; marginal path-product belief; authors state deeper branches remain exposed to calibration error.
per_position_analysis: Depth-1 calibration only; at first chain rejection the target token sits at draft rank 2-4 in 56-77%.
evidence: abs page; HTML Sec. 1, 3.3-3.4, 4 (Tables 1-4), 5, App. A.2, F, G
notes: ID correct. Not the earlier CAST (arXiv 2510.26577, cost-aware EAGLE trees). Its tree equals DDTree's top-N prefixes, yet DDTree/CaDDTree/BASTION are uncited. Under load the best static width is a wide tree up to B=8 and the plain chain from B=16; global best-first + varlen verifier beats the chain by median +7.0% (B=16) and +13.7% (B=32). T>0 uses SpecInfer/SpecTr recursive rejection.

title: TreeSpark: Calibrated, Load-Adaptive Draft Trees for Semi-Autoregressive Speculative Decoding
contribution: Evaluates DSpark's low-rank Markov head per concrete parent for parent-conditioned child distributions, Platt-calibrates them (2 scalars fitted on ancestors-accepted edges) into edge-acceptance estimates, and expands best-first by path survival until it falls below a price theta. Theta is looked up per round from a measured batch-size x temperature price ladder, and siblings drawn without replacement keep recursive rejection lossless at T>0.
limitation: Own: block depth b=7 caps per-round acceptance and the Markov head conditions only on the immediate parent (near-marginal deep in the tree). Wall-clock comes from a Python single-request harness; production batched goodput is unmeasured.
problem: Marginal trees mis-rank semi-AR drafts; fixed budgets ignore round difficulty and serving load.
reported_tau: 6.34 (Qwen3-4B, T=0, adaptive theta=0.02, block 7, 6-task held-out); 6.11 Qwen3-14B at N=56
targets_deep_positions: yes (limited); parent-conditioned edges keep branches coherent, but one-token Markov context fades with depth; block only 7.
per_position_analysis: No per-depth curve; text reports diminishing returns with depth.
evidence: abs page; HTML Sec. 1, 3.4-3.5, 4 (Table 1, Figs. 2-3), 5.1-5.5 (Tables 2-4), 6, App. Table 8
notes: ID correct; v1 12 Aug 2026 although the ID is 2609 (likely held). DDTree-style marginal trees on DSpark stay below the chain even at 8x budget. Load: at bs=16 and T>0 no branching tree beat the chain (ladder picks chain); at T=0, bs=16 a small tree gives +2.1%; fixed N=56 is net-negative; modeled adaptive is +7% over the best fixed shape at bs=64 (latency measured to bs=64; real engine used a 48-request pool). Raw q overestimates acceptance (0.62 vs 0.50).

title: From Chains to Trees: Parent-Conditioned Drafting for Semi-Autoregressive Speculative Decoding
contribution: Batches concrete frontier parents through DSpark's pretrained Markov head so each parent gets its own child ranking (top-k per parent), and keeps the most probable paths under a node budget N. Turns DSpark's chain into a tree with the same single backbone pass and no retraining.
limitation: Own: quality is bounded by the pretrained draft distribution, layer-wise top-k pruning is heuristic, and large k/N add non-negligible cost; gains depend on hardware, precision and kernels. Scope: greedy only, batch 1, single H20, fixed k=4, N=32.
problem: DSpark decodes one chain; an early mismatch kills the suffix, especially for large blocks.
reported_tau: 11.61 (Qwen3-14B, GSM8K, B=16, N=32, greedy; incl. bonus)
targets_deep_positions: yes; per-parent rescoring raises survival at depth 8 (57.1->64.8%) and 12 (40.3->46.8%); larger gains at B=16.
per_position_analysis: Accepted-depth survival S(d)=Pr[A>=d] to d=16, decaying; PCTree above the shared-Markov control at depth.
evidence: abs page; HTML Sec. 5.1-5.4 (Tables 2-4, Fig. 4), Sec. 6, App. A
notes: ID correct. B=7 uses official DSpark checkpoints; the B=16 drafters were trained by the authors with the DSpark recipe. Concurrent with TreeSpark (same Markov-head idea; TreeSpark cites it). Most cells are single runs. DDTree at N=32 reaches tau 7.49 on the same Qwen3-4B GSM8K setup.

title: DominoTree: Conditional Tree-Structured Drafting with Domino for Speculative Decoding
contribution: Scores DDTree's best-first heap with Domino's GRU causal correction recomputed along each candidate's realized root-to-node path (non-factorized scores), restricted to a marginal top-M candidate set. Adds a CUDA-graph builder and a host-sync-free, depth-synchronous frontier builder that runs as an out-of-tree SGLang plugin.
limitation: Own: on 16 GB cards the tree-verify buffer caps admission at 8-12 requests, so the chain wins goodput past that cap. A single fixed budget (16) is used, and the Domino drafter (trained to 3K tokens) limits long context.
problem: DDTree's factorized scores can't use Domino's path-dependent correction; Domino verifies one chain.
reported_tau: 12.86 (Qwen3-4B, GSM8K, T=0, budget-64 ablation); 8.09 overall on Qwen3-8B at budget 16
targets_deep_positions: yes; full-path GRU conditioning adds +4.7% tau over per-depth correction; long-context tau +29-36% over Domino.
evidence: abs page; HTML (v3) Sec. 1, 4.1, 4.5 (Tables 5-6), 6, App. A.1 (Table 8), A.3, D, Table 15
notes: ID correct (v3 Aug 2026). In SGLang (offered c=1-32; tree admission cap 8-12) the tau lead is +9% at every c, but Qwen3-8B goodput goes from +15.6% at c=1 to -0.3% at c=8, and stays within 2% on 4B. A CaDDTree-style adaptive budget saturates because path mass over-credits acceptance 1.07-1.16x. T>0 uses deterministic drafts with target sampling. Its frontier builder closely resembles DARTree's algorithm.

title: DARTree: Speculative Diffusion Decoding with Autoregressive Draft Trees
contribution: Expands a fixed width W of branches per depth, applying a pretrained causal correction head (Domino GRU or DSpark Markov) to all branches in one batch, then prunes the scored supertree to a global top-B with a depth bonus beta. This keeps path-specific correction while removing per-node heap/correction interleaving.
limitation: Own: it needs a drafter with a pretrained causal correction head, and tree verification adds compute, so it targets low-concurrency serving. Fixed large trees degrade under load (B=64 gives 1.06x AR at C=32).
problem: Path-conditioned correction inside best-first heaps forces slow sequential node-by-node expansion.
reported_tau: 12.97 (Qwen3-4B, GSM8K, T=0, B=64, W=12; 9.73x speedup)
targets_deep_positions: yes; per-branch correction plus a negative depth bonus puts nodes deeper; about half of GSM8K rounds accept nearly the full block.
per_position_analysis: Pr(L>=t) survival: DDTree stronger early, Domino later, DARTree both; mass piles up at block end.
evidence: abs page; HTML Methodology, Experiments (Tables 1-3, Figs. 4-5), App. A, B (Table 4), D (Fig. 7), F
notes: ID correct. Does not cite DominoTree although both build trees from Domino's GRU head. In SGLang at C=2-32 (App. B, RTX 6000 Ada, Qwen3-4B), a hand-set schedule (B=64/32/16/16/16, W=12/8/3/3/3) beats the Domino chain at C=32 by ~9% on GSM8K and ~14% on HumanEval at an equal 16-node verify size. The authors suggest longer draft blocks as future work.

title: Bastion: Budget-Aware Speculative Decoding with Tree-structured Block Diffusion Drafting
contribution: Grows a best-first prefix tree from DFlash marginals using a path-sum acceptance surrogate and stops at the first node where estimated speedup (surrogate x AR latency / roofline-calibrated cycle cost) decreases, which it proves unimodal. Tree size is query-dependent with no per-setting tuning.
limitation: Own: evaluation only at batch size 1 (larger batches change the verification-cost profile), and the offline latency calibration assumes a stable runtime profile.
problem: Static or fixed-budget diffusion trees ignore per-query hardware verification cost.
targets_deep_positions: no; marginal surrogate; best-first only deepens already-confident paths.
evidence: abs page; HTML Sec. 3.4, 4 (Table 1, Fig. 5), 5 (Figs. 6-7), App. A, H
notes: ID correct. Concurrent with DDTree (same best-first idea plus a cost-based stop); not compared to DDTree directly. Mean realized trees are ~87-202 nodes at bs=1. Verification is an exact match against the target's own token. Llama-3.1-8B uses a block-10 head; tested on A100/H100/A6000/RTX PRO 6000.

title: Cost-Aware Diffusion Draft Trees for Speculative Decoding
contribution: Replaces DDTree's fixed node budget with a per-round throughput objective using explicit drafting cost and a profiled, context-length-dependent convex verification cost. It proves surrogate throughput is unimodal, which gives a greedy stop inside DDTree's heap.
limitation: Scope (no limitations section): single-sequence harness on A800 GPUs, Qwen3-4B/8B only, block 16. It still scores nodes with factorized DFlash marginals (no path conditioning).
problem: DDTree's acceptance objective always favors bigger trees; no principled budget choice.
targets_deep_positions: no; only chooses how many marginal-ranked nodes to verify each round.
per_position_analysis: None per position; budget saturation analyzed by position-1 confidence decile.
evidence: abs page; HTML Sec. 4.1, 4.5-4.6, 5 (Tables 1-3, Figs. 3-5), App. C
notes: ID correct. Per-round mean budgets are 152-264 nodes (oracle grid picks 128/256). Batch size never mentioned; 1 inferred from the DDTree-style harness. DominoTree reports this rule saturates at its cap when draft probabilities over-credit acceptance.

title: TAPS: Target-Aware Prefix Tree Selection for Diffusion-Drafted Speculative Decoding
contribution: Trains a lightweight edge scorer (parent/child token, depth, draft log-prob, entropy) by distilling recorded target verification outcomes into sibling-normalized conditional acceptance, then multiplies along paths into reach probabilities. It greedily selects a prefix-closed subtree by utility reach/(lambda1 + lambda2*depth) under a budget and threshold.
limitation: Own: greedy T=0 only; a single-request prototype not integrated into vLLM/SGLang; it cannot recover target tokens missing from the drafter's top-K pool.
problem: Marginal-ranked diffusion trees verify unreachable descendants; large trees inflate verification latency.
reported_tau: 9.41 (Qwen3-4B, MATH500, A800, T=0); the DDTree-512 baseline reaches 10.52
targets_deep_positions: no; prunes unreachable deep descendants, and the utility penalizes depth (lambda2).
per_position_analysis: Top-8 marginals contain the target token 99%; budgeted trees lose 10-15% of correct tokens, mostly later positions.
evidence: abs page; HTML Sec. 3-5 (Table 2, Figs. 3, 6-9), Limitations
notes: ID correct (submitted 30 May 2026). Trades tau for speed: ~64-node trees, 1.36x over DFlash and 1.74x over DDTree-512; at a matched 64 nodes tau is 7.92 vs DDTree 6.93. The later GRAFT (2608.20375) uses the same idea (distilled edge scores + budget) without citing TAPS.

title: GRAFT: Adaptive DLM-Based Draft Tree Construction with Target-Distilled Edge Scoring
contribution: Adds a target-distilled, cacheable bi-tower parent-child compatibility residual (TDES; KL + pairwise + BCE losses on DDTree traces) to DFlash log-probs for edge scoring. Sets each round's budget by maximizing a fitted saturating-gain/affine-cost utility driven by draft confidence, hidden-state degeneration and acceptance history (SABA).
limitation: Own: drafting, tree construction and verification still run sequentially each round (pipeline bubbles). Scope: batch 1 on one A100, scorer trained per model on 3,046 prompts, and temperature and block size are not stated.
problem: DDTree attaches target-compatible tokens to wrong parents; fixed budget ignores decoding state.
reported_tau: 10.01 MAT (Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B, HumanEval); 9.68 Qwen3-4B Math500
targets_deep_positions: yes (limited); parent-child compatibility fixes mis-attached edges at every depth, but only conditions on the immediate parent token.
per_position_analysis: None for acceptance; notes DFlash adjacent hidden states grow more similar at later positions.
evidence: abs page; HTML Intro, Method, Experiments (Tables 1-3, Figs. 5-6), Conclusion
notes: ID correct; a different paper from Graft 2605.20104. v1 24 Jun 2026 although the ID is 2608 (likely held). Does not cite the earlier TAPS (same idea). Block size not stated (released DFlash heads), so max_draft_len is null; whether MAT includes the bonus token is unclear. SABA cuts the mean tree from 110 to 49 nodes; full GRAFT is +19.4% TPS over DDTree.

title: ECHO: Elastic Speculative Decoding with Sparse Gating for High-Concurrency Scenarios
contribution: Treats all requests' EAGLE-3 trees in a batch as one super-tree under a global verification-token cap, gating depth only at calibrated high-AUC 'sweet-spot' depths. Budget from truncated low-confidence requests deepens confident ones, and width is added only when no request can deepen; implemented in SGLang with CUDA graphs.
limitation: Scope (no limitations section): greedy decoding only, EAGLE-style drafters, and a warm-up to calibrate per-depth thresholds. High-load gains are measured against EAGLE-3 default trees, not against chains.
problem: Static trees waste verification at high concurrency; dynamic trees misjudge and break kernels.
reported_tau: 9.35 MAT (Vicuna-13B, HumanEval, BS=1, greedy)
targets_deep_positions: no; reallocates batch budget to deepen confident requests, but per-token draft accuracy at depth is unchanged.
per_position_analysis: Per-depth confidence of accepted vs rejected tokens: separable at root and few depths, overlapping and decaying deeper.
evidence: abs page; HTML (v2) Sec. 1, 3, 5 (Table 1, Fig. 5), App. C.4, D; icml.cc/virtual/2026/poster/64670
notes: ID correct; v1 10 Mar 2026 (ID 2604, likely held), v2 May 2026; listed in an ICML 2026 oral session. At BS>1 it starts from tiny trees (depth 3, top-3, 5 tokens) and gets +8% (LLaMA-3.1-8B) and +14.4% (Qwen3-235B) throughput over EAGLE-3 at BS=256. Vicuna MAT 9.35 exceeds the stated depth-8 cap +1 (unexplained).

title: TALON: Confidence-Aware Speculative Decoding with Adaptive Token Trees
contribution: Grows EAGLE-3 trees layer by layer under a global node budget: top-K at the root, then at each depth it keeps candidates whose cumulative path probability is within a factor mu of that depth's best. This yields deep-narrow trees in confident contexts and shallow-wide ones in uncertain contexts.
limitation: Own: evaluated only at batch size 1; at large batch, compute saturation plus per-request dynamic-tree and memory management become problems, and mu/N may need tuning.
problem: Fixed-width, fixed-depth EAGLE trees ignore per-token difficulty.
reported_tau: 9.48 MAT (Vicuna-13B, HumanEval, T=0, N=60)
targets_deep_positions: no; with no fixed depth cap, confident contexts grow deeper chains, but per-depth acceptance is not improved.
per_position_analysis: Acceptance funnel: depth 0 spread across top-K; deeper acceptance concentrates on top-1/2 candidates.
evidence: abs page; HTML Sec. 4-6 (Table 1), 8, App. B, E
notes: ID correct; same group as ECHO/Graft. Not the AAAI'26 'Talon' (hybrid model/retrieval drafting). An OpenReview entry exists with no decision found. No explicit max depth (budget 32-96 nodes); MAT 9.48 implies depth >8. T=1 uses EAGLE recursive rejection with residual resampling; T=0 is greedy.

title: Draft Less, Retrieve More: Hybrid Tree Construction for Speculative Decoding
contribution: Prunes EAGLE-3 trees at a few calibrated confidence checkpoints and grafts retrieved continuations into the released slots, keeping the total verification budget fixed. Retrieval reads a GPU-resident, online-updated token transition matrix through stage-specific templates.
limitation: Own: the SGLang high-batch version does not yet optimize retrieval kernels or scheduling. Scope: high-batch is only a Qwen3-8B sanity check up to BS=16 with a fixed tree shape, and the DFlash extension is preliminary.
problem: Dynamic-depth pruning discards valid branches, capping MAT below the dense-tree bound.
reported_tau: 8.53 MAT (Vicuna-13B, HumanEval, greedy); 6.64 with DFlash on Qwen3-8B GSM8K
targets_deep_positions: no; prunes uncertain deep branches and refills the slots with retrieved tokens.
evidence: abs page; HTML Sec. 2-4 (Tables 1, 5, 6, 13), App. B.4, C, D
notes: ID correct; distinct from GRAFT 2608.20375. At BS 1-16 (SGLang) it beats static EAGLE-3 trees by ~4-5% throughput; no chain baseline. Main results are greedy; the T>0 lossless argument is informal (retrieved tokens have no draft probabilities). Graft-DFlash gives +9.1% speedup over DFlash(16).

title: Yggdrasil: Bridging Dynamic Speculation and Static Runtime for Latency-Optimal Tree-Based LLM Decoding
contribution: Equal-growth trees (a fixed number of leaves per draft step, MLP-predicted depth, greedy width choice) keep shapes static for CUDA graphs/TorchInductor while maximizing a profiled latency-aware speedup objective. Adds DP verification-width pruning and stage-based ahead-of-time draft scheduling.
limitation: Own: results assume a single interactive request monopolizing the GPU, which does not apply to batched throughput-oriented serving. Scope: Llama-2-7B/13B with 68M/160M drafters; the depth predictor is trained per dataset and model pair.
problem: Dynamic trees break static compilation; AAL-maximizing ignores verification latency growth.
targets_deep_positions: no; predicts per-context depth but does not improve deep-position acceptance.
evidence: abs page (comments: Accepted by NeurIPS 2025); HTML Sec. 3-4, 7, 9
notes: ID correct. AAL appears only in figures. Fixed baseline tree is depth 16, width 8; best static config is D=8, W=8, verify 64. 'training' reflects the offline depth predictor; the drafter is off-the-shelf. Verification rule not described; temperatures >0 were tested.

title: Nightjar: Dynamic Adaptive Speculative Decoding for Large Language Models Serving
contribution: A contextual multi-armed bandit (context = current batch size) picks the chain speculative length gamma in {0..Gamma_max} each step, including gamma=0 to turn speculation off, with an explicit KV-rebuild switching cost. While speculation is off under memory pressure it offloads the draft model to CPU to enlarge the KV cache.
limitation: Own: switching-cost estimates come from offline profiling through a deployment-specific lookup table. Scope: chain drafts only, small separate drafters, vLLM on a single 4090/A100 (plus a 2-GPU 32B test).
problem: Fixed speculative length hurts under high load; an idle draft model wastes KV memory.
targets_deep_positions: no; shortens or disables the chain as load rises.
evidence: abs page; HTML (v5) Sec. 1, 5, 7-8 (Table 7), 10; Crossref DOI 10.1016/j.sysarc.2026.103889
notes: ID correct. NOT a tree method (chain gamma<=5, plus an appendix N-gram variant); relevant only as load-adaptive speculation that switches SD off when compute-bound. Max batch not reported (load up to ~35 req/s). It reports a per-token acceptance rate of 0.667 at mean gamma 2.43, not tau.

title: AdaServe: Accelerating Multi-SLO LLM Serving with SLO-Customized Speculative Decoding
contribution: Each iteration splits a hardware-profiled (roofline) global token budget across requests: it greedily adds the highest draft-path-probability nodes to each request until its expected acceptance meets its TPOT SLO, then fills the rest by global best-first. Candidate-tree depth and width scale with the number of active requests.
limitation: Scope (no limitations section): small same-family drafters (Llama-3.2-1B, Qwen2.5-0.5B) for 70B/32B targets on FlexFlow Serve. Per-request acceptance falls as RPS rises because each request's budget shrinks.
problem: Uniform batching and speculation can't meet heterogeneous per-request latency SLOs.
targets_deep_positions: no; shrinks depth and width under load to stay within the shared budget.
per_position_analysis: None measured; App. A assumes acceptance decays exponentially with depth.
evidence: abs page; HTML (arXiv v2) Sec. 3-6, App. A; ACM DL listing (doi 10.1145/3767295.3769315) via search
notes: ID correct; EuroSys'26 confirmed. The arXiv HTML carries the older title 'SLO-Customized LLM Serving with Fine-Grained Speculative Decoding'. Its batch-shared global best-first budget anticipates CAST/ECHO allocation. tau appears only in Fig. 12; depth bounds, batch sizes and the verification rule are not stated.

title: Acceleration Multiple Heads Decoding for LLM via Dynamic Tree Attention
contribution: Replaces Medusa's fixed tree with per-step top-n candidates under the product of the heads' top-m marginals, found with a priority queue (K=4, n=64, m=32); the selected set is automatically prefix-closed.
limitation: Own: about 10% slower wall-clock than Medusa (unoptimized), and the joint distribution is approximated by a product of marginals. Scope: Vicuna-7B on MT-Bench only.
problem: Medusa's fixed tree ignores context-dependent head confidence.
reported_tau: 3.51 tokens/step (Vicuna-7B, MEDUSA-2 heads, MT-Bench)
targets_deep_positions: no; depth fixed at 4 heads with marginal-product scores.
evidence: abs page; HTML Sec. 2-4, Table 1
notes: ID correct (title includes 'for LLM'). A preliminary note; its 'Speed up' column is tokens per inference. Losslessness is not established: the acceptance rule is unstated and MEDUSA-2 fine-tunes the backbone. It is the same product-of-marginals top-n idea that DDTree/BASTION/CAST later apply to DFlash (none cite it).

title: D-cut: Adaptive Verification Depth Pruning for Batched Speculative Decoding
contribution: Scores every draft position in the batch by its prefix-product drafter confidence (estimated survival probability) and verifies only a global top-K, so each request keeps a contiguous high-confidence prefix and low-confidence suffixes are pruned across requests. K is picked from {25,50,75,100}% of B(D+1) by maximizing estimated accepted tokens divided by a startup-profiled step-latency table C(B,rho).
limitation: Stated: per-step variable verify shape does not fit CPU-GPU overlap (Spec-V2) or full CUDA-graph capture, so it runs with piecewise graphs only. Scope: built on DFlash only, greedy draft proposals, concurrency <=64, H20/H800.
problem: Fixed-depth long block drafts waste compute-bound batched verification on rejected suffixes
reported_tau: 7.04 (D-cut-16, Qwen3.5-27B, HumanEval, conc. 32, greedy); unpruned DFlash-16 up to 7.87 (Qwen3-4B, Math500)
targets_deep_positions: no; it prunes low-survival deep positions under load rather than raising their acceptance.
per_position_analysis: No depth curve; prefix-product confidence vs acceptance is monotone (AUROC 0.96-0.97, Fig. 7); per-request MAT varies widely (Fig. 2a).
evidence: abstract; Sec. 1-4 (Table 1, Table 2, Figs. 4-5); Sec. 6; App. B, D (Table 5, Fig. 7)
notes: ID correct. Same Tencent team as AngelSpec, which reuses D-cut. MAT is reported only at conc. 32; there is no MAT-vs-concurrency data (MAT(K) is treated as hardware-independent). At conc. 32 DFlash-16 is below AR on all four dense targets (avg 0.67-0.98x) despite avg tau 4.6-6.4. App. B: confidence pruning that depends on the sampled token breaks losslessness under rejection sampling, so a shifted, non-anticipating score is needed.

title: AngelSpec: Towards Real-World High Performance Inference with Speculative Decoding
contribution: Domain-specialized drafters: (1) a shared-parameter MTP head trained with training-time test plus an LK-loss cold start and then an end-to-end TV (expected-accepted-length) loss, for chat; (2) DFly for code and math, a DFlash-style block-diffusion drafter with hybrid shared plus per-layer target conditioning and a predecessor-conditioned AR hidden-correction head. At serving time it adds D-cut cross-request verify pruning.
limitation: Scope: DFly only at block 8, concurrency <=64, 8xH20, Hy3/Qwen3-8B targets. Stated: the D-cut path runs piecewise CUDA graphs only and its selector is not free; live-traffic acceptance (~2.5) is far below benchmark tau.
problem: Parallel drafters suffer suffix acceptance decay; one drafter cannot fit heterogeneous workloads
reported_tau: 6.42 (DFly, Qwen3-8B, GSM8K, T=1, block 8); Hy3-A21B avg 4.79; ~2.5 on live Hunyuan traffic
targets_deep_positions: yes: MTP TTT lifts cumulative p3 0.266->0.524 with p1 ~unchanged; DFly AR head targets intra-block suffix decay.
per_position_analysis: Yes for MTP (Table 2): cumulative acceptance decays by position (T=0 after TTT 0.814/0.653/0.524); first position barely moves.
evidence: abstract; Sec. 2.3-2.5 (Tables 1-2), 3.4-3.5 (Tables 3-6), 4.4 (Table 7, Fig. 4), 5.4 (Table 8)
notes: ID correct (v2 Jul 29). Companion to D-cut (same authors). On live traffic, DFly mean AL is 2.50 averaged over c2-64 and also 2.50 at c64, so acceptance is flat with load; D-cut trims it to 2.43 at c64 for +15.7% throughput. Benchmark sweep (Table 7): the short MTP-3 nearly catches DFly-8 at c64 (2.08x vs 2.11x avg) after trailing badly at c4 (1.60x vs 1.98x). The conclusion contains a typo, 'Hy3-A20B'.

title: DScale: Scaling Block-Diffusion Speculative Decoding with Adaptive Verification
contribution: Keeps DFlash's drafter and full 15-token draft, but a separate 112K-parameter acceptance predictor (draft logits, hidden features, batch context) packs score-ranked per-request prefixes into half the native verify capacity (8N slots). It adds verify-specific attention tiles and fixed-address CUDA-graph workspaces that carry ragged request boundaries without CPU re-slicing.
limitation: Stated: only DFlash's 16-slot blocks evaluated; other widths left to future work. Scope: single A100-40GB TP1 (TP2 supplementary), Qwen3-4B/8B, math/code only, concurrency 8-32, mainly T=0.
problem: High-concurrency DFlash verification wastes padded tiles and slots on rejected candidates
reported_tau: DFlash full-width progress mean 6.09 incl. anchor (Qwen3-8B, mixed trace, c=8); 5.92 on GSM8K
targets_deep_positions: no; keeps long drafts but reallocates verify slots (retains ~91% of accepted tokens at half capacity).
per_position_analysis: No depth curve; per-request progress histogram (mean 6.09, tail to 16); mean logit gap vs acceptance Spearman ~0.73.
evidence: abstract; Sec. I, II-B, II-C (Figs. 2-4), IV-A to IV-D (Table I, Figs. 9-11), VI
notes: ID correct. The drafter is not retrained; only a 112K predictor per target-drafter pair is trained. Uniform truncation to width 8 cuts GSM8K progress 5.92->4.96 and throughput 15%, because a common cap truncates the long-tail acceptances. Gain over DFlash grows with concurrency (23% at c=8 to 60% at c=32) and it also beats DSpark (SGLang v0.5.16) and Domino. No acceptance-vs-concurrency data.

title: AdaFlash: Adaptive Speculative Decoding via On-Policy Distilled Diffusion Drafters
contribution: Online on-policy distillation of a DFlash diffusion drafter during serving: reverse-KL (entry-wise clipped) mixed with hard top-1 CE, using the target logits already computed in verification. A separately trained lightweight length head predicts each round's acceptance fraction and truncates the 15-token block; it is active only above concurrency 16 and can be scaled by load.
limitation: Stated: Qwen3.5-9B (GDN) gains narrow or reverse at C>=32 because SGLang varlen verify is immature. Scope: greedy by default (T=1 only at C<=32); the drafter adapts online to the served stream (cross-domain variant in appendix); GPU type not stated.
problem: Diffusion drafters show high domain/position acceptance variance; fixed k wastes verification
reported_tau: 9.83 (Qwen3-8B, MathQA, k=15, C=1, greedy) vs 7.09 for DFlash
targets_deep_positions: yes: on-policy distillation lifts acceptance at every position, most at later ones (Fig. 2c); tau 7.09->9.83.
per_position_analysis: Yes (Fig. 2c): DFlash per-position acceptance decreases monotonically with depth; OPD narrows the early-late gap.
evidence: abstract; Sec. 2.2, 3, 4.2 (Table 1, Fig. 2), 4.3; App. B.1, B.3 (Tables 5, 11)
notes: ID correct (v3 Sep 26). Key data point (Table 1): tau is flat from C=1 to 128 for EAGLE-3, DFlash and OSD (e.g. DFlash Qwen3-8B avg 5.86 at every C), which matches a flat acceptance-vs-concurrency measurement. AdaFlash's own tau drops only at C>=64 (7.28->6.88) because the length head truncates. Fixed k=15 DFlash falls to 0.76x at C=128 (Qwen3-8B) while AdaFlash holds 1.15x; on Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B it is 1.69x vs 1.02x.

title: An Interpretable Latency Model for Speculative Decoding in LLM Serving
contribution: Models request latency as C1/(1-RPS*C2), with batch inferred via Little's Law. SD enters through prefill/verify/draft costs amortized by E=(1-a^(k+1))/(1-a), plus an expert-coverage term for MoE. Speedup grows with load only if C2,SD/C2,dense<1, which happens only at very high acceptance, and larger k raises C2.
limitation: Stated: covers the stable pre-saturation regime and mean latency only; coefficients are system-specific (vLLM 0.13, A100/H100); adaptive drafting/trees may add cost terms. Scope: acceptance is synthetic (vLLM rejection sampler overridden) and assumed i.i.d.
problem: How SD speedup behaves under realistic load with emergent batch size
targets_deep_positions: no; analysis shows the k that is optimal at batch 1 is too long under load.
per_position_analysis: No; assumes constant per-token acceptance (geometric), synthetically enforced at 50-100%.
evidence: abstract; Sec. 3, 4.1-4.6 (Figs. 2-8), 5
notes: ID correct. Analysis paper, and its experiments are not lossless: acceptance is forced by overriding vLLM's rejection sampler, so acceptance cannot vary with load by construction. Batch is inferred from RPS and never reported as an integer. In their vLLM fits the load-dependent verify coefficient barely depends on k; the k cost enters mainly through the draft term.

title: Overcoming Joint Intractability with Lossless Hierarchical Speculative Decoding
contribution: A lossless sequence-level verifier: it scans the draft backward for the longest prefix acceptable under joint and capped-prefix ratios, then resamples once from a branch-level residual that balances excess and deficient mass within accessible next-token branches. This recovers the target distribution without intractable joint probabilities and drops into multi-draft (RRS) and EAGLE-3.
limitation: Scope: batch-size-1 implementation, single H20 (8xH20 for Llama-70B), GPTQ-8bit Qwen2.5 with a 0.5B draft; gains are modest (+3-12% block efficiency). Stated: with EAGLE-3's top-k drafting, verification degenerates, so EAGLE-3H gains come mostly from implementation speed.
problem: Token-wise verification under-accepts; sequence-level verification is intractable or lossy
reported_tau: 8.89 (HSD multi-draft, 11 drafts, Qwen2.5-72B/0.5B, GSM8K, T=1); single-draft 7.88 at gamma=15
targets_deep_positions: partly: sequence-level acceptance; relative gain grows slightly with draft length (+2.5% at gamma=5 to +3.5% at 15).
evidence: abstract; Sec. 1, 5.3, 6 (Tables 1-4); appendix code ('assume batch_size=1'); ICLR 2026 virtual site (oral)
notes: ID correct. The headline '>12% on EAGLE-3' is decoding speed: block efficiency rose only 3.40->3.55, which the authors attribute to sampling noise, since top-k drafting makes draft probabilities 1. Gains shrink at lower temperature (+0.7% block efficiency at t=0.6).

title: Speculative Speculative Decoding
contribution: The draft runs on separate hardware and, while a verification is in flight, pre-speculates for the most likely outcomes (accepted count plus bonus token) using a geometric fan-out cache over positions, so it can return a ready speculation on a hit. Saguaro sampling down-weights the cached top-F draft tokens to make the residual (bonus token) predictable, and a fallback switches to a fast speculator above a critical batch size.
limitation: Stated: SD is generally ineffective for throughput-bound workloads (large-scale RL, offline generation), and custom-mask attention limits profitable lookahead. Scope: batch <=16, greedy main results, custom engine plus one extra draft GPU.
problem: Drafting and verification remain sequential, so draft latency sits on the critical path
targets_deep_positions: no; it hides draft latency, and Saguaro sampling deliberately trades some acceptance for cache hits.
per_position_analysis: No data; theory assumes constant acceptance a_p (capped geometric accepted length) to size fan-out per position.
evidence: abstract; Sec. 1, 4.1-4.3 (Thms 12, 17; Figs. 3-6), 5, 6; App. B.2, E, F; PDF figure axes
notes: ID correct; ICLR 2026 per arXiv comment. K=2-12 appears only in baseline lookahead sweeps; SD/SSD runs propose 5 tokens, and no tau is reported. Batch-level cache-hit probability is p_hit^b, so misses become near-certain as batch grows and the whole batch stalls; gains are largest at low batch. App. E: with EAGLE-3 the pre-speculating draft conditions on up to 2K self-generated tokens, which lowers acceptance at later positions.

title: Global Resolution: Optimal Multi-Draft Speculative Sampling via Convex Minimization
contribution: Proves the canonical-decomposition and subset-selection views of multi-draft verification equal a relaxed optimal-transport LP. It reverse-engineers the problem into max-flow and, via polymatroid greedy flows and complementary slackness, reduces it to a truncated convex minimization in <=V variables, giving near-optimal acceptance for n i.i.d. drafts with tunable error.
limitation: Stated: i.i.d. drafts from one draft model only, single-step (multi-step only in a SpecTr appendix), and future work must cover non-i.i.d. drafts; the CPU solver can fail and takes up to 100 ms/token. Approximate: <=15*tau L1 deviation per token, so it is not exactly lossless.
problem: Optimal multi-draft verification LP has exponentially many variables; existing solvers suboptimal
reported_tau: 2.65 block efficiency (SpecTr + GR, Gemma-2 27B/2B, 4 i.i.d. paths, L=8, T=1); single-step acceptance ~90%
targets_deep_positions: no; single-position multi-draft acceptance; multi-step distribution error grows linearly in L (<=15*L*tau).
evidence: abstract; Sec. 1, 7 (Tables 1-2), 8; App. M, Q, R (Table 4, Thm R.1); ICLR 2026 proceedings/OpenReview
notes: ID found by search (none was given). The ICLR 2026 version is titled '... via Convex Optimization'. Not exactly lossless: there is an error tolerance. Batch size is not stated (solver runs on CPU). Acceptance rises with draft top-k up to ~1000 and with n<=10 at T=1; below T~0.8 a larger top-k rarely helps.

title: MoESD: Unveil Speculative Decoding's Potential for Accelerating Sparse MoE
contribution: Analysis showing that at moderate batch, once all experts are already activated, verifying extra draft tokens adds little MoE-FFN memory traffic. SD speedup on MoE therefore rises and then falls with batch, and the sweet spot widens with sparsity. It introduces 'target efficiency' T_T(B,1)/T_T(B,gamma) and a fitted roofline performance model.
limitation: Stated: assumes KV-cache volume is small relative to parameters (defers to MagicDec for the KV-dominated regime). Scope: gamma<=4, batch <=~100, vLLM, <=4 GPUs, no large expert-parallel deployments.
problem: SD thought ineffective for MoE; acceptance-centric evaluation ignores target-side cost
reported_tau: ~4.55 (= sigma 0.91 x (gamma+1); Qwen2-57B-A14B / Qwen2-0.5B, HumanEval, gamma=4, T=0)
targets_deep_positions: no; analyses verification cost vs batch, not acceptance.
evidence: abstract; Sec. 3.1-3.2, 4 (Tables 1-2, Figs. 2-4), 5; PDF figure x-axes (batch 0-100)
notes: ID correct. States that 'the acceptance rate across batch sizes merely fluctuates within a small range' while speedup swings, which matches flat acceptance vs concurrency. Max batch is read from figure axes (~100). The sparsity study edits num_experts_per_token, which changes the target.

title: Speculative Decoding: Performance or Illusion?
venue: MLSys 2026 (oral; Best Paper Honorable Mention per co-author page)
contribution: First systematic vLLM study of n-gram, EAGLE/EAGLE-3, draft-model and MTP SD at batch 1-128: target verification dominates step time, and acceptance varies within requests, across requests and across datasets. Oracle simulations quantify the gap to an upper bound that verifies only tokens that will be accepted, plus up to 2.2x more from per-position oracle choice between EAGLE and n-gram.
limitation: Scope: measurement study at temperature 0, mostly 3-token chains (n-gram 5; trees depth 3, k<=21), H100. Oracle bounds assume perfect acceptance prediction.
problem: Prior SD evaluations used research prototypes at batch size 1
reported_tau: 2.92 (EAGLE-3 tree k=21 depth 3, Qwen3-8B, GSM8K, SGLang) vs 2.25 for chain k=3
targets_deep_positions: no; points to oracle adaptive proposal length and method selection as future work.
per_position_analysis: By output-sequence position, not draft depth: tokens/step rise across long reasoning outputs (n-gram 1.6-3.7 to 2.7-5).
evidence: abstract; Sec. 3.1-3.2 (Table 1, Figs. 1-2), 5, 6 (Figs. 5-7), 8 (Figs. 10-12); MLSys 2026 oral page
notes: ID found by search (none was given). 20-token proposals are used only in the acceptance analysis; batch is 128 end-to-end and 512 in profiling. EAGLE speedup on Llama3.1-8B GSM8K falls 1.73x->1.21x from bs1 to bs128. The wide k=21 tree raises tau but drops below 1x by bs64 on all workloads, while chains stay above 1x. Output length varies with batch only through numeric nondeterminism; acceptance vs batch is not reported directly.

title: Correctness Forensics for Batch Speculative Decoding: Diagnosing the Ragged Tensor Problem
contribution: Shows published batch-SD implementations (BSP, DSD) silently corrupt outputs. It formalizes two invariants needed for output equivalence under contiguous KV layouts (rectangular alignment; position-ID/KV contiguity), enforces them without custom kernels (EqSpec), and groups same-length sequences across batches to skip realignment (EXSpec).
limitation: Stated: contiguous-KV setting only (not integrated into vLLM/SGLang); benefit is confined to moderate batch because realignment overhead grows superlinearly (~38-40% at BS=32); 90.8-97.3% exact match (fp nondeterminism); EXSpec trades tail latency for throughput.
problem: Batched SD implementations report speedups while violating output equivalence
targets_deep_positions: no; correctness and systems work.
evidence: abstract; Sec. 1, 4.1-4.3 (Tables 2, 5, 6; Fig. 5); Limitations; App. F
notes: ID correct but retitled: v1-v3 were 'Batch Speculative Decoding Done Right', and v4 (Aug 31 2026) took the current title. Useful as a correctness checklist (exact/partial match vs non-spec) for any new batched algorithm. Paged/varlen engines such as vLLM v1 avoid the ragged-tensor problem by construction.

title: SwiftSpec: Ultra-Low Latency LLM Decoding by Scaling Asynchronous Speculative Decoding
contribution: Disaggregates draft and target onto separate tensor-parallel GPU groups that run concurrently. The draft keeps growing a maximum-likelihood token tree, re-rooted after each verification with tree-aware KV reuse, while the target verifies an 8-token subgraph each round; fused GEMM+all-reduce and attention kernels cut small-batch TP latency.
limitation: Stated: hard to apply to EAGLE-style drafters (they need target features), and the int4 latency kernels are unsuited to high-throughput serving (batch >=64). Scope: single request only, with 4-bit AWQ targets.
problem: Draft latency on critical path; draft/target TP scaling imbalanced at small batch
reported_tau: 3.92 accepted guesses/verify (Qwen2-72B/1.5B, HumanEval, parallel tree); serial 4.20 (GSM8K)
targets_deep_positions: no; async drafting lowers acceptance ~9% (draft blind to in-flight verify), offset by hiding latency.
evidence: abstract; Sec. 2.3, 3.1, 5.1-5.5 (Table 6), 6; ACM DL ASPLOS'26 listing
notes: ID correct. Published as 'SwiftSpec: Disaggregated Speculative Decoding and Fused Kernels for Low-Latency LLM Inference' (ASPLOS'26). Tree depth is dynamic with 8 tree tokens verified per round (7 layers in the motivation study), so draft length is left null. The target samples along the tree; temperature is unstated. 348 tok/s on Llama3-70B with 8xH800.

title: Beat the long tail: Distribution-Aware Speculative Decoding for RL Training
contribution: A training-free drafter built from a per-problem suffix tree (incremental Ukkonen) over a sliding window of recent rollouts, so it tracks policy drift. A length-aware budget derived from a latency model (c_base*N_fwd + c_tok*N_toks) gives long/straggler requests aggressive draft budgets and disables speculation for short ones.
limitation: Scope: <=14B models (results on 7B/8B), VeRL, T=0.6, math/code RL; budgets use a heuristic 3-class predictor and no acceptance numbers appear in the text. Stated: prefix-routing CPU overhead can outweigh gains for small models.
problem: Long-tail rollouts dominate RL step time; static drafters go stale under drift
targets_deep_positions: no direct mechanism; gives long requests larger budgets, and suffix matches can yield long accepted bursts.
per_position_analysis: No measurement; App. C assumes acceptance decays exponentially with round depth.
evidence: abstract; Sec. 4.1.2, 4.2, 5 (Figs. 4, 6, 7, 10-13); App. C; MLSys 2026 oral page
notes: ID correct. 256 is the effective per-GPU rollout batch for math RL (128x16/8); code RL uses 16-32. Rollout time drops >50% (math) and ~25% (code). The unlimited-budget variant is 15% worse, so overly long drafts hurt even as the rollout batch shrinks. Acceptance improves over training as the tree refreshes, while EAGLE stays flat.

title: ReSpec: Towards Optimizing Speculative Decoding in Reinforcement Learning Systems
contribution: Adapts EAGLE-3 SD to RL rollouts. An offline-profiled solver/scheduler switches SD configurations (steps s, branching t, draft tokens n), or disables SD, as the active batch shrinks. The drafter is continuously distilled from the evolving actor with reward-weighted KD, with updates overlapped asynchronously with generation.
limitation: Scope: Qwen2.5 3B-14B, math GRPO only, VeRL+SGLang, 2x8 H100. Its claim that plain EAGLE-3 degrades RL reward conflicts with lossless verification and is not explained, which suggests an implementation-specific non-exactness.
problem: SD speedup vanishes at large RL batch; drafter goes stale as actor updates
targets_deep_positions: no; keeps drafter aligned to the moving actor; aggressive configs used only at small active batch.
evidence: abstract; Sec. 3, 4.1 (Figs. 3, 4, 6, 7), 5.2-5.3, 6.1 (Figs. 12-13); PDF figure text; MLSys 2026 oral/poster pages
notes: ID found by search (none was given). Fig. 7: the best config at batch 2 gives 1.46x but the same config gives 0.76x at batch 32, and the most aggressive (5,8,32) gives 0.45x at batch 64. The RL active batch decays from ~16 to ~1 in the long tail. The draft length of 5 is the SGLang step depth s; n (up to 32) is total draft tokens. EAGLE-3 acceptance length falls from ~4 over 100 RL steps (plot only, so tau is null).

title: Taming the Long-Tail: Efficient Reasoning RL Training with Adaptive Drafter
contribution: A single-layer EAGLE drafter is retrained continuously on GPUs idled by long-tail rollouts (spot trainer) to track the evolving policy. A rollout engine with bucketed pre-captured CUDA graphs uses an epsilon-greedy bandit (BEG-MAB) to pick draft depth and verify width by running-request count, enabling SD only when fewer than ~32 requests remain; a model-free n-gram drafter covers early steps.
limitation: Scope: GRPO reasoning RL on Qwen2.5-7B/32B and Llama-70B; SD is used only below ~32 running requests. Stated: EAGLE-3/HASS were rejected because training-time-test training is too costly inside rollout bubbles.
problem: Long-tail rollouts idle GPUs; static drafters misalign with the evolving RL policy
skill: spot-trained adaptive drafter, bandit SD tuning
reported_tau: 8.67 (Qwen-32B, EAGLE tree depth 12, 64 verify tokens, topK 8, BS=1, T=0)
targets_deep_positions: yes: continual drafter training keeps acceptance at distant draft positions far above a stale drafter (Fig. 16).
per_position_analysis: Yes (Fig. 16): accept rate by draft index 1-8 decays; stale drafter collapses at later indices, adaptive sustains.
evidence: abstract; Sec. 5, 6.3-6.6 (Tables 1, 4, 6-8; Figs. 13-16); ACM DL / GitHub (ASPLOS'26)
notes: ID correct. Table 4 (Qwen-32B, depth 10): the best verify width shrinks with batch (64 tokens at bs1 gives 3.62x; at bs32, 16 tokens gives 2.48x vs 1.70x with 64). A 128-request rollout uses SD only in the tail, for 2.44x overall. The adaptive drafter lifts AL 4.59->6.53 on the RL-trained target.

title: Accelerating RL Post-Training Rollouts via System-Integrated Speculative Decoding
contribution: Integrates lossless SD (EAGLE-3, native MTP or draft models) into NeMo-RL's vLLM rollout backend for sync and async RL, computing log-probs and loss against the verifier policy. Online drafter adaptation reuses the policy forward's cached hidden states through a detached path, and a GB200 simulator projects gains to 235B scale.
limitation: Scope: real runs only at 8B (Qwen3-8B), 32 GB200s, math GRPO; the 235B / ~2.5x end-to-end results are simulator projections. Speedup is capped by non-generation stages (Amdahl bound).
problem: Rollout generation bottlenecks RL; existing speedups perturb the on-policy distribution
reported_tau: 5.06 (EAGLE-3 k=7, Qwen3-8B-Base RL-Zero rollouts); 3.32 at k=3
targets_deep_positions: no; longer drafts raise AL but cut speedup (k=5 and k=7 are slower than AR on RL-Think).
notes: ID correct. The real-run rollout batch is not stated (the simulator uses a global rollout batch of 4096). On RL-Zero, k 3->7 raises AL 3.32->5.06 but drops speedup 1.77x->1.21x; RL-Think goes 1.53x->0.71x. n-gram (AL 2.05-2.47) is slower than AR. In-domain drafter initialization matters more than online adaptation.

title: Windowed-MTP: Removing the Full-Context Draft-KV Tax at Million-Token Context
contribution: Applies a StreamingLLM sliding window (4032 tokens) plus a 64-token attention sink to the built-in MTP/NEXTN draft head's attention only, leaving full-attention verification untouched. This bounds the draft's KV read at 1M context to a constant, and a ring buffer reclaims the unread draft KV (7.7-11% of total) for extra batch capacity.
limitation: Stated: gain scales with the draft's windowable cost share; headline numbers are B=1/TP1 in SGLang and framework-relative; lossless only in exact arithmetic (bf16 batched-verify noise); the acceptance mechanism is strongest at d=7. Scope: 1M-token long-prompt/short-answer inputs, greedy decoding.
problem: At 1M context, MTP draft attention dominates step cost; deep drafts turn net-negative
reported_tau: 5.9 (native MTP, Qwen3.6-35B, RULER niah_multivalue, 1M, d=7); windowed up to 4.76
targets_deep_positions: no; preserves (sometimes slightly raises) deep-position acceptance while cutting draft cost, making deeper drafts profitable.
per_position_analysis: Yes (Table 9): conditional alpha_j ~0.9 flat to j=6 for Qwen-122B; decays for Qwen-35B (0.53) and Nemotron (0.20).
evidence: abstract; Sec. 1, 3, 5 (Fig. 2), 6 (Tables 2-3, Figs. 4-5), 7 Limitations; App. C (Tables 9-10)
notes: ID correct; single author. d=9 means 8 draft tokens (d=7 <-> gamma=6); native d=9 OOMs at 1M for the 122B and Nemotron models. Batch sweeps (B<=6 at TP1, B<=13 at TP2) are reported cost-side only because AL is not bit-stable across TP. On the lowest-AL workload (Nemotron+FWE), dense wins peak throughput at high batch.

title: [Spec Decode] DSpark confidence-scheduled verification
contribution: A Triton kernel ranks draft slots by survival probability (cumulative product of EMA-smoothed per-position confidence) and admits the prefix that maximizes estimated accepted tokens per ms, using step-cost curves profiled with dummy steps at startup. The batch budget is sized on CPU from stale double-buffered confidences (no sync), per-request allocation runs on GPU, and decode CUDA graphs become varlen.
limitation: PR-stated: output logprobs are rejected when enabled, and non-SM100 GPUs fall back to piecewise graphs without the varlen full-graph win. Scope: one model (DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark, TP4, B300), one internal prompt set, and the no-spec arm ran on a shared node.
problem: Fixed 7-token speculation falls below no-spec once the GPU saturates
reported_tau: ~3.9 (DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark, 7 drafts, T=1); 3.5 at c=256 with adaptive trimming
targets_deep_positions: no; deliberately trims deep drafts as verification gets expensive (AL 3.9->3.5 at c=256).
evidence: GitHub PR #47808 description (merged 2026-08-12, created 2026-07-07); DSpark abstract (arXiv 2607.05147)
notes: Not a paper; the companion DSpark paper is arXiv 2607.05147 (DeepSeek, Jul 2026). Adaptive is within +-3% of fixed-k at c<=64, while at c=256 fixed 7-token is 33% below no-spec and adaptive keeps a win. The AL drop is deliberate trimming, not a load effect on acceptance. GSM8K 0.945/0.951 (c=16/64); probabilistic draft sampling, T=1.

title: EAGLE-3: Scaling up Inference Acceleration of Large Language Models via Training-Time Test
contribution: Drops feature regression for direct token prediction from fused low/mid/high target features, trained with 'training-time test' that feeds the drafter its own multi-step predictions. Acceptance then keeps improving with more drafter training data.
limitation: No limitations section; caveats: gains shrink with batch (SGLang 1.38x at bs 64, vLLM ~1.01x at bs 56) and 405B/671B targets untested. Serving runs used chains of only 2-3 tokens.
problem: Feature-prediction loss limits data scaling; later steps see unseen self-predicted features
reported_tau: 7.54 (Vicuna-13B, HumanEval, T=0, tree depth 8)
targets_deep_positions: yes: TTT trains on self-predicted inputs so later-step conditional acceptance stays near first-step level.
per_position_analysis: Yes, Fig. 7 n-alpha (conditional on accepted prefix): EAGLE-3 'almost unchanged' with n; EAGLE declines (LLaMA-3.1-8B, MT-bench).
evidence: abstract; HTML Sec. 4.1 Fig. 7 (n-alpha), Fig. 1 (data scaling), Table 5 (SGLang/vLLM batch); NeurIPS 2025 proceedings
