notes: Anchor. Earliest report of ~flat conditional acceptance with depth (AR drafter, <=7 steps, values only in figure). KVShot (2604.26412) and Attention Drift (2605.09992) find decay on Qwen3-8B and beyond the TTT horizon.

title: Beyond Parallel Blindness: Information Floors and Model Gaps in Block Drafting
contribution: Splits per-slot block-drafter rejection into an information floor (minimum TV risk given which earlier tokens are seen) and a model gap, with estimators on 4 open targets. Uses it to replace DSpark's predecessor correction with a prefix-attention head.
limitation: Main analysis at gamma=7 (gamma=16 only in an appendix replication on Qwen3-4B); estimator biases acknowledged and component gains come from one-epoch runs. The new drafter gains only ~4% over DSpark.
problem: Accepted length cannot separate missing within-block information from imperfect drafter modeling
reported_tau: 5.32 (Qwen3-4B, 9-task mean, T=0, SGLang, block 7, 3.76x)
targets_deep_positions: yes (analysis): all-parallel floor rises to 0.47 at slot 15; one seen predecessor removes 81-98% of it.
per_position_analysis: Yes: DFlash free-rollout risk 0.24->0.64 (slots 1-6) but reached-path risk flat ~0.17-0.22, i.e., constant conditional acceptance.
evidence: abstract; HTML Sec. 2-3 (Figs. 2, 4, 5), Table 1, Table 7, App. C.4 (gamma=16 floors), App. F.2, App. H.4 (c=1-32)
notes: Closest match to the researcher's observation. Model gap = 43-64% of DFlash final-slot rejection. Tau load-invariant (DSpark 5.18 at c=1 and c=32). Joint-survival tau 4.57 vs 3.40 from product of marginals (positive dependence).

title: When Hidden States Drift: Can KV Caches Rescue Long-Range Speculative Decoding?
contribution: Diagnostic framework comparing hidden-only, target-KV-only and hybrid context reuse in EAGLE-3-style drafters. Argues the target's last hidden state is a query-biased compression that drops information later steps need; target-KV reuse raises late-step acceptance.
limitation: Stated: end-to-end gain marginal (HF MAT 5.04 vs 5.01) with 5-10% extra drafting latency; shallow drafters can't estimate target queries and draft-side KV projections get sparse gradients. Qwen3-8B only, no wall-clock speedup.
problem: Long-range acceptance decay persists even in TTT-trained hidden-state drafters
reported_tau: 5.04 (Qwen3-8B, HF MAT, tree depth 8/top-10/60 tokens); step-wise MAT 2.54 vs 2.37 EAGLE-3
targets_deep_positions: yes: KV reuse lifts step-6 acceptance (4-layer KV-only 0.495 vs EAGLE-3 0.469) but hurts step 0.
per_position_analysis: Yes: conditional alpha_k, k=0..6; EAGLE-3 decays 0.638->0.469 (73.5% retention); hybrid 0.665->0.514 (Qwen3-8B).
evidence: abstract; HTML Sec. 4 step-wise table (alpha_0/3/6, retention), Sec. 5 (bottlenecks)
notes: Contradicts EAGLE-3's flat n-alpha on Qwen3-8B. Suggests block-wise training as the fix (not verified). Related: ConFu (2603.08899) feeds target 'future' signals; long-draft survival test at DL=12.

title: Attention Drift: What Autoregressive Speculative Decoding Models Learn
contribution: Shows EAGLE-3 drafters and MTP heads shift attention from the prompt to their own recent tokens because hidden-state magnitude grows monotonically with chain depth. Post-norm on drafter states plus RMSNorm on captured target features keeps deep steps stable beyond the TTT depth.
limitation: Stated: focus on EAGLE-3 (MTP drift observed, fix untested there) and models <120B. Post-norm with short TTT trails pre-norm TTT-8 in overall accepted length (5.05 vs 7.12).
problem: Drafter state norm grows with chain depth, drifting attention and collapsing beyond TTT horizon
reported_tau: 7.12 (EAGLE-3 pre-norm TTT-8, HumanEval/GSM8K, 20-step chain); SGLang best 5.89 (Qwen3-8B, MATH-500)
targets_deep_positions: yes: post-norm keeps conditional acceptance stable past training depth (TTT-2: 0.53 vs 0.00 at step 16).
per_position_analysis: Yes (Fig. 10): conditional acceptance 0.91 (step 1) -> 0.50 (step 16) for TTT-8; pre-norm TTT-2 collapses to 0.
evidence: abstract; HTML Table 1 (RMS growth), Table 2, Fig. 10 (verbatim checked), Sec. 4.2-4.3
notes: Up to 2x tau under template perturbation, 1.18x long context, 1.10x standard benchmarks. Position-specialist layers for later positions: PosS (2506.03566).

title: LK Losses: Direct Acceptance Rate Optimization for Speculative Decoding
contribution: Losses that target per-position acceptance alpha = 1 - TV directly: -log(alpha), and a KL/TV hybrid whose weight exp(-eta*alpha) is set per draft position from running acceptance (KL early, TV later). Drop-in for EAGLE-3, MLP speculator, Medusa and DeepSeek MTP.
limitation: Stated: only chain sampling with sequential acceptance; trees, block verification and direct tau optimization left to future work. Gains small for strong drafters at T=0 (DeepSeek-V3 MTP +0.8% mean).
problem: Capacity-limited drafters minimizing KL converge to points that don't maximize acceptance
reported_tau: 5.72 (DeepSeek-V3 MTP, GSM8K, T=0, K=7); largest mean gain +8.2% (Qwen3-235B, T=1)
targets_deep_positions: partly: per-position adaptive weighting; gains reported larger for longer drafts (tau vs K, Fig. 1).
per_position_analysis: No per-position table; notes original MTP shows sharp acceptance decline at later positions.
evidence: abstract; HTML Sec. 3 (loss definitions), Table 1, Fig. 1, Table 4, Limitations
notes: Six targets 8B-685B. BV Loss (2609.34832) reports beating LK by ~16% tau on DFlash under block verification.

title: Acceptance-Aware Draft Model Training for Speculative Decoding
contribution: Window losses equal to expected accepted length via cumulative prefix products: EAL for greedy (probability of target argmax) and WTV for sampling (1 - TV of temperature-scaled distributions). Optional GRPO stage uses simulated accepted length as reward.
limitation: No limitations section; greedy gains are tiny (5.088 vs 5.057) and a CE baseline beats KL at T=1, cutting WTV's margin to ~0.16 tokens. Batch 1, gamma<=7, standalone small-LM drafters only.
problem: CE/KL distribution matching does not directly optimize acceptance length
reported_tau: 6.67 (Qwen3-32B target / Qwen3-4B drafter, tree, T=1, WTV) vs 5.96 KL
targets_deep_positions: partly: prefix-product loss weights later positions by survival; no position-specific analysis.
evidence: abstract; HTML Sec. 3 (EAL/WTV/GRPO), results tables (median/P25/P75 tau)
notes: Includes Gemma4-31B target with Gemma4-E2B drafter. Assumes per-position acceptances conditionally independent given prefix. GRPO stage reuses GTO's reference debiasing.

title: BV Loss: Block Verification-Aware Loss for Block Diffusion Speculative Decoding
contribution: Derives the drafter loss 1 - E_BV[tau]/B from the block-verification acceptance rule (cumulative q/p ratios), so training maximizes expected sequence-level accepted length; reduces to TV loss at B=1. Gains also transfer to token-wise and greedy verification.
limitation: Stated: only parallel block drafters; AR drafters and tree schemes (Traversal Verification) left to future work. Single seed, 256-token generations, thinking off, batch 1.
problem: Drafter objectives are token-level while verification credits only accepted prefixes
reported_tau: 7.28 (Qwen3-4B, DSpark, GSM8K, BV, T=1); mean 5.43 (Qwen3-8B, DSpark, 4.00x)
targets_deep_positions: yes: raises conditional extension at all 15 positions; DFlash position-8 retention 21.8% -> 33.2%.
per_position_analysis: Yes: conditional extension improves at all 15 positions; final position 0.776 -> 0.838 (DFlash, Qwen3-4B, GSM8K, T=1).
evidence: abstract; HTML Sec. 3 (loss), main tables, per-position retention/extension figure (verbatim checked), Limitations
notes: +13-21% tau over CE under BV; ~+16% over LK on DFlash; pure TV training failed (tau ~1-2). B=15 drafted + anchor. Related losses: D-PACE (2605.18810), Spec-AUF (2607.01893), Teaching Diffusion to Speculate L2R (2606.11552).

title: Training Parallel Speculative Draft Models by Directly Minimizing Expected Decoding Rounds
contribution: Casts SD with block/semi-AR drafters as a Markov reward process over (round start, verified position) states, giving an objective exactly equal to expected decoding rounds and an unbiased TD-style gradient from target rollouts. Captures cross-round coupling and yields an exact offline round-count evaluator.
limitation: Stated: fixed block size (adaptive sizing for high-concurrency serving open) and costlier than block-local objectives. Measured gains small (<= +0.04 MAL over E2E, <= +0.13 over released drafters), B=7, no serving runs.
problem: Block-local surrogates ignore that round starts depend on earlier rounds' acceptance
reported_tau: 6.35 MAL (Qwen3-8B + DFly, GSM8K, T=1, offline estimator)
targets_deep_positions: no: optimizes global round count; proves per-round tau maximization can be suboptimal.
per_position_analysis: Defines offline per-position acceptance estimator AR_k; no per-position results in text read.
evidence: abstract; HTML Sec. 3 (MRP, EDR objective, Theorem 3), results tables, Limitations (first 100K chars read)
notes: Theorem 3: for B>=3 a first-order drafter maximizing per-round accepted length can lose MAL by factor >1+1/(3B+9). Posted 2026-10-07.

title: Verification-Aware Training for Speculative Decoding
contribution: Simulates verification each training step: a jointly trained verification head predicts whether each position survives sequential verification, and per-position loss weights stay at 1 up to the sample's first rejection, restarting the decay there. Plug-in for EAGLE-3 and DFlash.
limitation: Stated: evaluated only up to 8B models. Some T=1 regressions (DFlash LLaMA GSM8K 4.87 -> 4.64) and DFlash training memory 23.8 -> 31.5 GB.
problem: Fixed per-position loss weights ignore that verification discards tokens after first rejection
reported_tau: 8.71 (DFlash+VAT, Qwen3-8B, GSM8K, T=0); EAGLE-3+VAT 8-bench mean 6.78 (Qwen3-4B, T=0)
targets_deep_positions: yes: rejection-anchored weighting moves the first-rejection point later during training (Fig. 2a).
per_position_analysis: No acceptance-by-position curve; reports first-rejection position shifting later and post-rejection target matches.
evidence: abstract; HTML Sec. 3, main results tables, Figs. 2-3, Limitations
notes: NAVER AI. Also applied to EAGLE-3 (AR head). Up to +11.4% tau (DFlash Qwen3-8B 5.51 -> 6.14). HF Transformers on A100; serving batch not reported.

title: Bridging Draft Policy Misalignment: Group Tree Optimization for Speculative Decoding
contribution: Draft Tree Reward = expected acceptance length of the decoding-time draft tree under the target (sampling-free), optimized with reference-debiased, group-standardized advantages and a PPO-style surrogate along the longest accepted path.
limitation: Stated: extra training compute (~200/400/900 A100 GPU-hours for 8B/13B/70B). Batch 1 only and tree depth <=8.
problem: Training optimizes one greedy path while decoding verifies a re-ranked tree
reported_tau: 7.95 (Vicuna-1.3-13B, HumanEval, T=0) vs 7.33 EAGLE-3
targets_deep_positions: no: optimizes whole-tree expected length; no depth-specific mechanism.
per_position_analysis: No per-position rates; accepted path equals greedy path only 36-49% of the time.
evidence: abstract; HTML Sec. 3, main results table, Fig. 2, App. E; OpenReview dwPdYFqVWO / ML Anthology ICLR 2026
notes: +7.4% tau, +7.7% speedup over EAGLE-3 (T=0). First widely followed RL/acceptance-objective drafter training.

title: Draft-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Speculative Draft Models
contribution: On-policy distillation for drafters: target-assisted SD rollouts give stable continuations, then drafting is replayed from every block anchor so the target scores draft-induced states (forward KL on accepted, decayed reverse KL on rejected tokens). Breaks the SFT plateau.
limitation: Stated: only Qwen3 targets and DFlash-style drafters; thinking-mode rollouts capped at 4096 tokens vs 8192 at eval. First-rejection mass shifts only slightly toward later positions.
problem: SFT on fixed target trajectories plateaus; drafter is evaluated on its own draft states
reported_tau: 6.68 (Qwen3-4B thinking, MATH-500, SGLang); 7.64x speedup (Qwen3-8B, GSM8K, T=0)
targets_deep_positions: weakly: first-rejection share at positions 7-15 rises only 28.5% -> 29.5% during training.
per_position_analysis: First-rejection histogram over 16-token blocks peaks at position 2 (~14%) and declines toward 15.
evidence: abstract; HTML Sec. 3, Table 1, Figs. 1/4, App. D, SGLang concurrency results
notes: +23% over EAGLE-3, +13% over DFlash for thinking models; gains hold at SGLang concurrency 32. Off-policy label fix for block drafters: Recovering Off-Policy Supervision (2609.38795, +36.5% greedy tau over DFlash; abstract only, HTML 404).

title: Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding
contribution: At every drafter layer a gated adjacent injection writes position t-1's predicted feature into position t, so the causal chain unfolds over network depth while all positions update in parallel. Features live in a whitened transfer space built from target output embeddings.
limitation: No limitations section; only Qwen3-4B/8B, thinking off, block 16. Speedups shrink with concurrency (Qwen3-8B 1.59-1.81x over AR at c=32).
problem: Independent parallel positions yield inconsistent continuations, shortening the accepted prefix
reported_tau: 7-bench mean 4.82 vs DFlash 3.77 (Qwen3-8B, T=0); best 5.67 (GSM8K)
targets_deep_positions: yes: correct predecessors help later positions most (gain grows at positions 4->8->12); injected early in depth.
per_position_analysis: No DSpine curve; DFlash diagnostics show predecessor-correction gains grow with position.
evidence: abstract; HTML Sec. 3-4, main tables (vs Domino/DSpark), SGLang serving (c=2-32)
notes: +23.3% SGLang throughput over DFlash. Baselines retrained in-paper; absolute tau not comparable across papers. Other coherence heads: LiLiCorr (2608.20530), DBLAST (2608.05448), Weaver (2607.06763), D-Loop (2610.06011), DeLS-Spec (2607.07409).

title: Carryover Drafting: Recycling Rejected States for Speculative Decoding
contribution: Recycles target hidden states computed at rejected positions as temporary, read-only drafter KV context (one learned tag embedding, replaced each round), with parallel draft-verify-draft training that exposes the drafter to inference-aligned rejected states.
limitation: Stated: not tested with confidence scheduling or tree decoding; trains single-round retention only and adds training compute; fixed verify length. One block size (15 proposed tokens), two targets.
problem: Verifier computation on rejected tokens is discarded though it encodes future tokens
reported_tau: 7.91 (Qwen3-4B, DSpark-style Markov drafter, Math, T=0; 6.52x vLLM bs 1)
targets_deep_positions: yes: gains start at position 0 and persist across the block (recall@1 +1.3-5.6 points).
per_position_analysis: Yes (matched-anchor replay): carried states better at every position; values only in figure.
evidence: abstract; HTML Sec. 3-4, main tables, per-position replay figure, concurrency table (c=1-32), Limitations
notes: Targets Qwen3-4B and Gemma 4 12B. Relative gain mostly holds at c=32 (+7.6-11.5%). Concurrent rejected-suffix reuse: DFlow (2609.06498), ReTrace (2608.29748).

title: DFlare: Scaling Up Draft Capacity for Block Diffusion Speculative Decoding
contribution: Replaces DFlash's single fused target feature with per-draft-layer softmax mixtures over 9 target layers (separate K/V projections for target context), so deeper drafters keep improving; scales training data from 800K to 2.4M samples.
limitation: Stated: high training cost (32 GPUs, ~100-160 h per drafter) and data beyond 2.4M unexplored. Depth tested only to 7 layers; extra depth barely moves speedup.
problem: Single fused target feature bottlenecks per-layer expressiveness and drafter scaling
targets_deep_positions: no: no explicit late-position mechanism beyond a progressive position-weighted loss.
evidence: abstract; HTML Sec. 3, Tables 4-6 (target layers, depth, data), SGLang concurrency table, Limitations
notes: Scaling: Qwen3-8B tau 4.90/6.59/7.33 at 270K/800K/2.4M samples (diminishing); Qwen3-4B tau 6.55->6.90 for 5->7 layers. Tencent AngelSlim.

title: Ceiling-Clipped Acceptance Histograms Indicate Stranded Speed-up in Block-Diffusion Speculative Decoding
contribution: Shows high-acceptance block drafters often accept the entire block ('stranded speed-up', a spike in the acceptance histogram's ceiling bin) and that naive inference-time widening hurts. DBloom post-trains B16 drafters to B24 with a curriculum emphasizing the new offsets.
limitation: Stated: narrow grid (Qwen3-8B/4B, two drafters, one Gemma target), in-sample correlation over ~5 drafters, ablations on Qwen3-8B only; larger blocks future work. Inference concurrency not reported.
problem: Fixed trained block horizon caps accepted length when whole blocks are accepted
reported_tau: 10.54 (Qwen3-8B, DFlare B24, MATH-500); Qwen3-4B 10.39
targets_deep_positions: yes: extends trained horizon 16->24; naive widening erodes front positions (DFlare-4B tau 7.54->3.45).
per_position_analysis: Models survival as product of per-position alpha; splits change into tail gain minus front erosion.
evidence: abstract; HTML Table 1 (naive B24), Arm A/B results, per-position decomposition section, Limitations
notes: Includes Gemma-4-12B-IT (median +0.41 tokens). Gains concentrate on high-ceiling math; MT-Bench only 5.38 at B24.

title: Scaling Laws for Speculative Decoding
contribution: Fits log-linear laws of drafter acceptance vs drafter pretraining tokens and drafter depth, plus throughput vs batch size with a batch-dependent optimal tree top_k. Builds Scylla, an EAGLE-style drafter pretrained on 10B tokens with scaled decoder layers.
limitation: Stated: drafter RLHF unexplored, larger drafters add compute, dense Transformer settings only, code unreleased. Pretraining gains saturate beyond ~50B tokens; acceptance vs batch not measured.
problem: Unknown how drafter data, capacity and batch size govern acceptance and speed
reported_tau: 6.90 (Scylla, Vicuna-13B, HumanEval, T=0)
targets_deep_positions: no: scales overall drafter quality; no position-specific analysis.
evidence: abstract; HTML Theorems 1.1-1.3, Tables 4/5/9, batch-size experiments (Qwen2.5-72B)
notes: Fits: tau ~ 0.74*log10(layers)+4.61; 0.08*log10(pretrain tokens)+5.05 (units unclear). 1.21x over AR at b=64. Drafter pretraining follow-up: Osprey (2609.09338, EMNLP 2026, +16-23% tau). Draft depth not stated.

title: Test-Time Speculation
contribution: Shows speculator acceptance collapses with output length on long reasoning traces, then adapts the drafter per request online with one gradient step per (strided) round, using the verifier's logits as a free teacher (position-weighted KL plus drift regularizer).
limitation: Stated: unfused PyTorch gradient kernels, fixed update stride, SGLang CUDA-graph/autograd integration issues. Batching not evaluated; drafter reset between requests.
problem: Offline-trained drafters degrade on outputs far longer than training sequences
reported_tau: 4.9 vs 2.9 DFlash (Qwen3.5-122B, AIME 2025; +72%)
targets_deep_positions: no: targets decay along output length, not draft depth.
per_position_analysis: None by draft position; by output length DFlash AL falls 15 -> 1.7 within 25K tokens (Qwen3.6-35B, AIME-2025).
evidence: abstract; HTML Sec. 2 (Fig. 2 degradation), Sec. 3-4, App. C
notes: UT Austin. Drafter CE on target top-1 rises 2.8 -> 6.4 nats over long outputs. Other online drafter updates: OnlineSPEC (2603.12617, ICML 2026), Aurora (2602.06932), TIDE (2602.05145, SC'26).

title: SuffixDecoding: Extreme Speculative Decoding for Emerging AI Applications
contribution: Model-free drafting from suffix trees over prompts and past outputs, with speculation length set by pattern-match length (MAX_SPEC = alpha*p). Hybrid mode uses suffix drafts when their estimated accepted-length score exceeds a threshold, else falls back to EAGLE-3.
limitation: Paper notes weak results on open-ended, high-entropy text (Spec-Bench, WildChat); hybrid helps there (2.5x vs EAGLE-3 2.4x) but trails suffix-only on agentic tasks. Mostly batch 1.
problem: Agentic workloads repeat long spans that model drafters speculate too briefly
reported_tau: 7.82 tokens/step (Llama-3.1-8B, SWE-Bench, suffix-only; 17.14 on sphinx subset); hybrid 7.5 (AgenticSQL)
targets_deep_positions: yes for repetitive text: speculates up to alpha x match-length tokens when long matches exist.
evidence: abstract; HTML Sec. 4 (hybrid, threshold sweep), AgenticSQL/SWE-Bench/Spec-Bench tables, vLLM end-to-end
notes: Hybrid anchor (v1 2024-11; hybrid in NeurIPS version). Concurrency inconsistent (8 tasks in figure, 16 workers in appendix). 2026 hybrids: Graft (2605.20104), WhiFlash AR/diffusion routing (2606.07710, EMNLP 2026), APEX (2610.07780), AgSpec (2610.01108).

title: KVBuffer: IO-aware Serving for Linear Attention
contribution: Buffers recent keys/values of linear-attention layers so decode runs chunkwise with deferred, batched state updates, and SD drafts are verified in parallel chunkwise form, with the state updated only from accepted tokens' KVs (no per-draft temporary states).
limitation: Scope: only Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B (MTP chain, 4 draft tokens end-to-end) on 4x L40S in SGLang. Stated: no dynamic routing between computation forms; chunkwise decode can be slower than recurrent at batch 1.
problem: Per-draft temporary recurrent states multiply memory/IO and cap hybrid SD concurrency
targets_deep_positions: no
evidence: arXiv abstract; HTML Secs. 3.3, 4.1-4.2 (Figs. 4-5), 6
notes: Up to 5x more max serving requests and 1.46x SD throughput at 4 draft tokens; 2.78x verify-kernel speedup at 8 drafts. Max batch 128 is from the short-context KV-only test. Acceptance rule unchanged and tau not reported.

title: Trees from Marginals: Autoregressive drafting with factorized priors
contribution: A 56.7M-param autoregressive adapter (Weaver) re-scores DFlash's top-K per-position marginals, conditioned on the tokens already drafted (no full-vocab projection), to grow best-first proposal trees verified by Traversal verification. Also adds a rollback-free GDN tree-verify kernel (masked triangular solve; commit replays the accepted path).
limitation: Stated: the serving path handles one request at a time; depth is capped by DFlash's 16-token block; the tree is built from draft probability, not acceptance. Scope: one target (Qwen3.6-27B bf16, 1x B200).
problem: Factorized drafters' independence assumption makes acceptance decay sharply with draft position
reported_tau: 9.69 macro (T=0) / 9.35 macro (reasoning), max 13.61 on one code task; Qwen3.6-27B, budget-64 tree, bs 1
targets_deep_positions: yes: conditions each position on the realized draft tokens, beating any marginal drafter's acceptance at later positions.
per_position_analysis: Yes (Fig. 4): acceptance vs position 1-15. Marginal/DFlash rates decay; TfM stays higher at late positions. Chain tau saturates (Fig. 6).
evidence: arXiv abstract; PDF Secs. 1.2, 3.5 (Fig. 4), 4.2-4.3, 5.1 (Table 2), 6
notes: 'Weaver' is the adapter; the full system is called DFlash-TfM. Tree budgets 32-512 swept. Claims +77% MAL vs the DFlash chain, +32% vs DDTree at equal tree size, and 4.37x over AR. No arXiv HTML, so the PDF was read.

title: SpecLA: Efficient Speculative Decoding for Linear-Attention Models
contribution: Topology-aware GDN verification kernels (serial state-resident, tree-masked parallel, chain-decomposed hybrid). Buffers compact verification factors to recover only the accepted state with a fused delayed commit, and prunes an EAGLE-style drafter's tree by a path log-prob margin.
limitation: Scope: one pure-GDN 1.3B target on one H100, greedy, <=128 new tokens, batch size not stated; best 1.70x end-to-end (1.06x on HumanEval).
problem: Transformer SD runtimes ignore recurrent state dependencies across chains and branches
reported_tau: 5.00 (GDN-1.3B, GSM8K, greedy, tree; chain 3.47)
targets_deep_positions: no
evidence: arXiv abstract; HTML Secs. 6, 8.1-8.5 (Fig. 9, tree-shape table), 9
notes: The target is pure linear attention, not a hybrid. Output hashes checked identical to AR (FP32 state). Depth 24 comes from the tree-kernel study; the synthetic chain study uses L<=12.

title: Bole: Efficient Tree Speculation for Hybrid-Attention Language Models
contribution: Exact closed form for gated-delta-rule tree verification: an ancestor-masked system whose inverse is a depth-bounded nilpotent polynomial, run in a value-tiled kernel. Stores token-level factors and rebuilds only the sampled path's state; sets a batch-wide node budget by profiling the full hybrid forward pass.
limitation: Scope: Qwen3.5 4B-122B with native MTP (top-k 4, depth 8) on A100 and GB10 in SGLang; end-to-end batch <=8 (kernel B=16). The budget needs offline per-config profiling, and MAT gain over baselines is ~0.1 token.
problem: Branch-by-branch recurrent verification and per-node state snapshots scale with tree x batch
reported_tau: 7.08 MAT (Qwen3.5, GSM8K, MTP tree, bs 4)
targets_deep_positions: no
evidence: arXiv abstract; HTML Secs. II-C, IV, V, VI (Tables I, III, V-VII)
notes: Baseline snapshots take 36 GiB for eight 32-node requests on Qwen3.5-122B. Bole cuts transient state 82-99x and is up to 2.03x faster than the best tree baseline (GB10, bs 8). Concurrent with TreeWY.

title: TreeWY: Speculative Verification for Gated DeltaNet Hybrids
contribution: Tree-structured WY/UT transform of the gated delta rule: one triangular solve yields every draft node's output. Only the accepted state is reconstructed at commit, from a small pseudo-value matrix, instead of keeping per-position state snapshots (vLLM fork).
limitation: Stated: wider trees raise acceptance but are not yet a throughput win (tree verify can't be graph-captured; depth capped at 3); 1-3% slower where memory does not bind. Scope: Qwen3.5-35B/397B, depth-3 MTP, greedy, B200.
problem: Per-draft GDN state snapshots cap concurrency and make wide trees memory-infeasible
reported_tau: 2.786 (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, depth 3, width 3; store-all 2.868)
targets_deep_positions: no: adds width; acceptance stays capped by depth 3.
per_position_analysis: Per-depth acceptance matches baseline within 0.01; per-position rate falls as width grows (App. B).
evidence: arXiv abstract; HTML Secs. 2, 4-6, Tables 1-2, 4; App. B, D
notes: Not bit-identical to baseline (bf16 tolerance). Up to 1.49x throughput and ~40x lower p99 TTFT where memory binds. In App. D, ReplaySSM gets more chain throughput at equal memory (1.12-1.20x vs 0.99-1.08x).

title: LumoTree: Path-Parallel Speculative Verification for Hybrid Language Models
contribution: A shared tree descriptor drives path-parallel GDN verification (reused recurrent tiles, boundary states for dependent paths). The accepted path is replayed through native fused GDN updates, with coordinated conv-history gathering and KV remapping. Adds fused MTP spine/sibling selection plus suffix-lookup tails.
limitation: Stated: one active sequence (batch >1 not covered by results); no bitwise or strict greedy equality established; 10-task agent study. Scope: Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 on one DGX Spark (GB10).
problem: Hybrid tree speculation must commit consistent recurrent, conv and KV state
reported_tau: 4.35 accepted drafts per spec. step vs 3.17 for MTP-5 (Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4, GB10, T=0.6)
targets_deep_positions: no: suffix lookup extends depth to 11 beyond 5 MTP passes; no depth-specific acceptance mechanism.
evidence: arXiv abstract + v1/v2 abs pages; HTML Secs. VI, VII-A to VII-H, IX
notes: v1 title: 'GDN Tree-Scan: Served Tree Verification for Recurrent-Hybrid Language Models'. v3 re-measured after fixing the sampler's per-path penalty histories. On replay corpora it is 7.7-11.8% faster than MTP-5 in tok/s; SGLang EAGLE is comparable or faster (agent run 26.1 vs 29.9 tok/s).

title: SketchSSM: Write to the Full State, Read from a Compact Sketch
contribution: Keeps exact full-state updates (ReplaySSM-style buffered flushes) but approximates per-step state reads with a low-rank sketch. At each flush it precomputes state outputs for an offline-fixed query basis; reads are then reconstructed from query-dependent coefficients.
limitation: Scope: lossy read approximation that needs offline rank calibration; evaluated for standard decode only (no speculative decoding); speedups measured on B300 at batch 128-512.
problem: Buffered-update methods still read the full recurrent state every decode step
targets_deep_positions: no
evidence: arXiv abstract; HTML Secs. 1-3, 5 (Figs. 1, 6-7)
notes: Not a speculative-decoding paper (0 mentions) and not lossless. About 10x less state traffic at mean rank 8; kernels 3.2-3.7x faster than ReplaySSM at bs 512; up to 2.77x decode throughput on Nemotron 3 Super.

title: H-Spec: Parallel Speculative Decoding Without a Drafter-Side KV Cache
contribution: Hybrid Mamba-attention block drafter. The Mamba state is initialized from projected last-position target hidden states (an O(1) context summary), attention layers reuse the target KV in place (no drafter KV cache), and a DSpark Markov head follows. Mamba's parallel scan keeps drafting block-parallel.
limitation: Stated: drafter K/V dims must match the target's; drafting is slower at low concurrency or short inputs. Scope: 4-8B Transformer targets on one A100, <=7 draft tokens, chain only.
problem: Block drafters' separate drafter KV cache grows memory and KV-write cost with concurrency
skill: Mamba init from target hidden state
reported_tau: 4.29 (Llama3.1-8B-IT, code task, bs 1, T=0.6, k=7); 8-task avg 3.08-3.24
targets_deep_positions: partly: hybrid injection recovers later-position acceptance lost by KV reuse; margin over DSpark grows with k (~4% to ~9%).
per_position_analysis: Yes (Fig. 4): conditional acceptance by position; KV-reuse-only drops up to 16.5 pp by index 6, ~0 at 0-1.
evidence: arXiv abstract; HTML Secs. 2-5 (Fig. 4, Table 2); App. C.3
notes: 'Hybrid' refers to the drafter (Mamba+attention); the targets are plain Transformers. Higher throughput at lower KV use from 8 to 128 concurrent requests.

title: Component-Aware Self-Speculative Decoding in Hybrid Language Models
contribution: Uses a hybrid model's own SSM/linear-attention subgraph as a zero-parameter drafter, with attention zeroed or skipped via hooks. Shows the perplexity ratio under attention ablation predicts acceptance.
limitation: Stated: the research Python implementation is slower than AR (0.009-0.50x wall clock); models <=3B; chain verification only. Sequential hybrids (Qwen3.5) reach only alpha~0.04.
problem: Self-speculation had ignored hybrid models' internal component heterogeneity
targets_deep_positions: no
per_position_analysis: Reports all-k-accepted rate alpha(k) at k=2/4/8; decays (Falcon-H1-0.5B 0.68, 0.37, 0.19).
evidence: arXiv abstract; HTML Secs. 4-5 (Tables 3-4, 7), 7
notes: Title found for the given id (correct). No real speedup (all measured wall-clock <1x on one L4). Tau only plotted (Fig. 1b). Viable for parallel hybrids (Falcon-H1), not for sequential ones (Qwen3.5).

title: Super Apriel: One Checkpoint, Many Speeds
contribution: A 15B supernet with four trained mixers per layer (FA/SWA/KDA/GDN), switchable per request. The all-FA placement can verify drafts from a cheap placement (e.g., all-GDN) of the same checkpoint; the draft placement is chosen via an offline acceptance estimator plus surrogate search.
limitation: Stated: fast presets regress on long-range retrieval (RULER/NIAH); single teacher (Apriel 1.6). Scope: SD speedups are estimated from teacher-trace acceptance (gamma=8), not measured end-to-end.
problem: Separate draft models must be trained and loaded; hybrid presets lose quality
targets_deep_positions: no
evidence: arXiv abstract; HTML Sec. 7.6 (Fig. 11), Sec. 8, App. J.2

title: Tail-Replay: Escaping the Curse of Linear Attention in Prefix Caching for Hybrid LLMs
